articles.title: Comunidades indígenas de Boa Vista iniciam colheita de milho | G1
articles.standfirst: Com apoio da Prefeitura, foram plantados 102 hectares neste ano, apesar dos efeitos do El Niño
articles.summary: Com apoio da Prefeitura, foram plantados 102 hectares neste ano, apesar dos efeitos do El Niño
articles.body:
: A Serra do Truaru colheu os grãos cultivados na comunidade, após meses dedicados à lavoura — Foto: PMBV

Resultado do trabalho em equipe, a colheita de milho na área indígena marca uma importante etapa na produção agrícola de Boa Vista. Nessa quarta-feira, 23, com o apoio da prefeitura em todas as etapas do processo de cultivo (preparação do solo, aquisição e distribuição de insumos e plantio), a Serra do Truaru colheu os grãos cultivados na comunidade, após meses dedicados à lavoura.

Neste ano, foram plantados 102 hectares de milho nas comunidades do município, dentro da janela de cultivo, fator que impacta diretamente na produtividade da safra. De acordo com o secretário de Agricultura e Assuntos Indígenas, Cezar Riva, a prefeitura investe para manter o campo mais forte e capaz de impulsionar o desenvolvimento agrícola da capital.

“Com o potencial produtivo das comunidades indígenas, a prefeitura segue investindo para garantir que esses agricultores produzam em maior quantidade e com mais qualidade, aumentem sua renda e tenham mais segurança para permanecer no campo. Cada hectare colhido significa alimento na mesa e geração de oportunidades para os agricultores indígenas da capital” , disse.

Neste ano, foram plantados 102 hectares de milho nas comunidades do município, dentro da janela de cultivo — Foto: PMBV

As famílias produtoras da Serra do Truaru colheram 8 hectares de milho plantados em parceria com a Prefeitura. Para a coordenadora do projeto de grãos da comunidade, Keila da Silva, chegar ao momento da colheita, após meses de trabalho intenso, é gratificante, já que esse momento representa o resultado de todo o empenho, dedicação e cuidado dos produtores ao longo do ciclo de cultivo.

“Recebemos os técnicos da Prefeitura e as máquinas para preparar o solo na área que a gente vai plantar. Depois, continuam com a gente em todos os processos até chegar o dia da colheita. Hoje estamos aqui colhendo o resultado de meses de trabalho. Agora, uma parte da nossa colheita vai ser vendida e a outra fica na comunidade para alimentar os animais” , contou.

: Keila da Silva é coordenadora do projeto de grãos da comunidade — Foto: PMBV

Com assistência técnica especializada e a disponibilização de máquinas agrícolas, os agricultores conseguem reduzir os custos operacionais e aumentar a produtividade das lavouras durante a colheita. Integrante do projeto de grãos da Serra do Truaru, Robermário da Silva é claro: sem o apoio da prefeitura, a comunidade não conseguiria cultivar a área de plantio sozinha.

“Hoje, contamos com as máquinas e os técnicos para ajudar a gente. Se fosse trabalhando na mão, não seria possível plantar no tempo certo, nem colher essa quantidade de milho que estamos colhendo aqui. A ajuda da prefeitura é muito importante para a comunidade conseguir fazer essa colheita. Os técnicos estão sempre nos acompanhando no tempo certo” , destacou.

Com assistência técnica especializada e a disponibilização de máquinas agrícolas, os agricultores conseguem reduzir os custos operacionais e aumentar a produtividade das lavouras durante a colheita — Foto: PMBV

A colheita ocorreu mesmo após a forte estiagem registrada no mês de julho, que tem afetado o desenvolvimento de parte das lavouras em todo o estado. As chuvas desse período são essenciais para o enchimento dos grãos, e a ausência de precipitações comprometeu a produtividade em algumas áreas. Os impactos estão relacionados aos efeitos do El Niño.

O fenômeno climático associado ao aquecimento das águas do Oceano Pacífico, influencia o regime de chuvas na região Norte. De acordo com o Instituto Nacional de Pesquisas Espaciais (INPE), a previsão para o segundo semestre de 2026 indica a intensificação do período seco. Em Boa Vista, a estiagem deve provocar perdas de aproximadamente 50% em relação ao que foi colhido na mesma área no ano de 2025.

articles.title: Cleitinho Azevedo propõe maior divulgação de destinos turísticos de MG | G1
articles.standfirst: Candidato do Republicanos ao governo de Minas Gerais cumpriu agenda em Belo Horizonte nesta quarta-feira (30).
articles.summary: Candidato do Republicanos ao governo de Minas Gerais cumpriu agenda em Belo Horizonte nesta quarta-feira (30).
articles.body:
Cleitinho Azevedo (Republicanos) no Mercado Central nesta quarta-feira (30) — Foto: TV Globo/ Reprodução

O candidato do Republicanos ao governo de Minas Gerais, Cleitinho Azevedo, cumpriu agenda de campanha no Mercado Central, em Belo Horizonte, na tarde desta quarta-feira (30). Ele estava acompanhado de aliados políticos e apoiadores.

Cleitinho percorreu os corredores do mercado, entrou em lojas e conversou com comerciantes e clientes. Ele também posou para fotos com eleitores e experimentou produtos típicos.

O candidato apresentou propostas voltadas ao fortalecimento do turismo e do comércio em Minas Gerais, como a ampliação da divulgação dos destinos turísticos do estado e o incentivo à atividade econômica nos municípios.

A ideia é que o aumento do fluxo de visitantes impulsione setores como hotelaria, bares, restaurantes, lojas e prestadores de serviço, gerando mais movimentação econômica nas cidades. Cleitinho não quis gravar entrevista.

A visita ao Mercado Central foi o único compromisso público previsto na agenda de campanha do candidato nessa quarta-feira.

articles.title: Ônibus bate em poste às margens do Rio Paraibuna, em Juiz de Fora | G1
articles.standfirst: Acidente aconteceu na noite desta quarta-feira (30), na avenida Brasil. Condutor disse tentou desviar de uma moto.
articles.summary: Acidente aconteceu na noite desta quarta-feira (30). Condutor disse tentou desviar de uma moto.
articles.body:
Um ônibus do transporte coletivo, da linha 712, bateu em um poste na avenida Brasil, na altura do bairro Cerâmica, antes do viaduto da BD, em Juiz de Fora , na noite desta quarta-feira (30). Conforme informações do Corpo de Bombeiros, uma pessoa que estava no coletivo ficou levemente ferida.

Ainda segundo a corporação, o motorista disse que foi fechado por um motociclista e desviou para não causar um atropelamento. Devido à chuva e à pista escorregadia, acabou perdendo o controle da direção e batendo no poste, que caiu sobre o veículo.

Houve rompimento da fiação elétrica, que entrou em curto-circuito. A rede precisou ser desergizada pela Cemig para que os passageiros pudessem descer em segurança.

Ônibus bateu em poste próximo ao bairro Cerâmica, em Juiz de Fora — Foto: Rodrigo Soares/TV Integração

À TV Integração , a Cemig informou que dois clientes tiveram o fornecimento de energia interrompido. No entanto, havia relatos de outros locais sem luz, incluindo o terminal rodoviário Miguel Mansur.

Devido à batida, o trânsito ficou muito congestionado na avenida Brasil, em direção à Zona Norte.

articles.title: Incêndio consome estátua na Pedra da Feiticeira em SP; VÍDEO | G1
articles.standfirst: Corpo de Bombeiros foi acionado no fim da tarde desta quarta-feira (30), em São Vicente. Estrutura de fibra de vidro, com cerca de 3,5 metros, foi consumida pelas chamas.
articles.summary: Corpo de Bombeiros foi acionado no fim da tarde desta quarta-feira (30), em São Vicente. Estrutura de fibra de vidro, com cerca de 3,5 metros, foi consumida pelas chamas.
articles.body:
Um incêndio atingiu a estátua da Feiticeira, localizada na Pedra da Feiticeira, em São Vicente , no litoral de São Paulo, nesta quarta-feira (30). Segundo o Corpo de Bombeiros, a estrutura foi consumida pelo fogo. Ninguém ficou ferido.

Ainda de acordo com a corporação, a equipe foi acionada por volta das 17h50 para atender à ocorrência na Avenida Ayrton Senna, no bairro Itararé. No local, os bombeiros encontraram a estátua, de aproximadamente 3,5 metros de altura e construída em fibra de vidro, atingida pelas chamas.

Os bombeiros utilizaram água de um caminhão para controlar as chamas. As chamas foram extintas e o local foi deixado em segurança. O policiamento de área também foi acionado para adotar as medidas administrativas necessárias.

O g1 procurou a Prefeitura de São Vicente, mas não obteve retorno até a última atualização desta reportagem.

Incêndio atingiu a Pedra da Feiticeira, em São Vicente. — Foto: Reprodução

A formação rochosa fica na Praia do Itararé e é conhecida por uma lenda que deu origem ao nome. Segundo as histórias, uma mulher misteriosa costumava passar a noite no local, conhecido como “Cama da Velha”.

A lenda conta que ela era apaixonada por um marinheiro português, que partiu prometendo voltar, mas nunca mais apareceu. Certo dia, ao acreditar que alguém em um barco distante acenava para ela, a mulher entrou no mar em direção à embarcação e morreu afogada. A escultura da feiticeira era assinada pelo artista Francisco Telles.

Fogo atingiu a Pedra da Feiticeira em São Vicente. — Foto: Victor Godoy e Reprodução

articles.standfirst: Cícero Lucena (MDB), Efraim Filho (PL), Lucas Ribeiro (PP), Camilo Duarte (PCO) e Yuri Ezequiel (UP) cumpriram agenda pública nesta quarta-feira (30).
articles.summary: Cícero Lucena (MDB), Efraim Filho (PL), Lucas Ribeiro (PP), Camilo Duarte (PCO) e Yuri Ezequiel (UP) cumpriram agenda pública nesta quarta-feira (30).
articles.body:
Candidatos ao Governo da Paraíba — Foto: Arte/g1

Os candidatos ao governo da Paraíba cumpriram agenda em João Pessoa e outras cidades no nesta quarta-feira (30). Os compromissos de campanha incluíram caminhadas, encontro com empresários e também com o setor da educação no estado.

O primeiro turno de votação será em 4 de outubro. O segundo está marcado para o dia 25 do mesmo mês.

Veja, abaixo, como foi o dia de campanha de cada candidato:

O candidato ao governo da Paraíba pelo MDB, Cícero Lucena, cumpriu agenda em João Pessoa, Bayeux e Cabedelo . Pela manhã, ele fez gravações para o guia eleitoral.

A agenda do candidato Cícero Lucena seguiu, no fim da tarde, com uma caminhada no bairro do Cristo Redentor, na capital. Depois, ele seguiu para a cidade de Bayeux, onde participou de evento político. À noite, ele participa de uma plenária em Cabedelo, na Região Metropolitana.

O candidato ao governo da Paraíba pelo Partido Liberal (PL), Efraim Filho, cumpriu agenda de campanha em João Pessoa. Durante a manhã, o candidato participou de um encontro no sindicato dos plantadores de cana de açúcar.

Ainda nesta data, ele continuou a agenda com a gravação de guia eleitoral.

O candidato à reeleição ao governo da Paraíba, Lucas Ribeiro (PP), começou a manhã desta quarta-feira (30) cumprindo agenda adminsitrativa, depois, reuniu-se com representantes da construção civil e do mercado imobiliário, no Sindicato da Indústria da Construção Civil (Sinduscon), no bairro de Tambauzinho, em João Pessoa.

À tarde, Lucas Ribeiro cumpriu outra agenda administrativa. No fim da tarde, participará de uma atividade de campanha em Lucena, na Região Metropolitana de João Pessoa. À noite, o candidato tem como compromisso uma concentração com eleitores na Praça das Muriçocas, no bairro de Miramar, em João Pessoa.

Pela manhã, o candidato Camilo Duarte fez panfletagem no Bairro das Industriais, na capital. Na sequência, ele seguiu para dois outros atos de entrega de material de campanha em dois bairros também de João Pessoa.

À noite, ele participou de ato de Rui Costa Pimenta, na Rua Afonso Pena, 333, em Santo Amaro, no Recife.

O candidato Yuri Ezequiel cumpriu agenda de campanha, no bairro de Jaguaribe, pela manhã. Na sequência, participou de panfletagem na Epitácio Pessoa, também na capital. À tarde, ele teve conversa com trabalhadores da indústria de Santa Rita

No final da tarde, ele fez panfletagem na Universidade Federal da Paraíba (UFPB).

articles.title: Gabriel defende crédito para agricultores e recuperação de estradas | G1
articles.standfirst: Candidato do MDB ao governo de Minas Gerais teve compromissos em BH e Região Metropolitana nesta quarta-feira (30).
articles.summary: Candidato do MDB ao governo de Minas Gerais teve compromissos em BH e Região Metropolitana nesta quarta-feira (30).
articles.body:
Gabriel (MDB) em encontro no Crea-MG — Foto: TV Globo/ Reprodução

O candidato do MDB, Gabriel, fez campanha em Belo Horizonte e na Região Metropolitana nesta quarta-feira (30).

Gabriel começou o dia participando de uma reunião com diretores do Conselho Regional de Engenharia e Agronomia de Minas Gerais (Crea-MG), na Região Centro-Sul de Belo Horizonte. Ele recebeu uma carta com demandas da categoria.

O candidato disse que, se eleito, vai realizar concursos públicos para servidores das áreas de engenharia e de geociência. Em relação ao campo, afirmou que pretende criar equipes de técnicos para atender as demandas de municípios por meio de governos regionais. Propôs, ainda, planos de saneamento e recuperação de estradas rurais para garantir o escoamento da produção.

Gabriel falou ainda que vai disponibilizar crédito aos agricultores e preparar o setor para enfrentar eventos extremos ligados às mudanças climáticas.

"Primeiro lugar, não pode faltar crédito. Infelizmente, o crédito diminuiu nesse governo. Vamos retomar. Segundo, estrada boa, porque senão a comida fica cara, chegando na mesa de quem vai consumir depois de muito buraco. Terceiro, tem que ouvir o homem do campo e respeitá-lo. Gente que acorda cedo antes da gente para garantir alimento para Minas Gerais", afirmou.

Ainda pela manhã, Gabriel participou de um encontro no Conselho Regional de Administração de Minas Gerais (CRA-MG), em Belo Horizonte. Durante a tarde, o candidato realizou caminhadas na capital e em Nova Lima.

articles.title: Vale registra aumento de mortes violentas em agosto e no acumulado do  | G1
articles.standfirst: Aumento foi de 46,7% comparado ao ano passado.
articles.summary: Aumento foi de 46,7% comparado ao ano passado.
articles.body:
Dados divulgados nesta quarta-feira (30) pela Secretaria de Segurança Pública mostram que o Vale do Paraíba teve aumento no número de mortes violentas, que incluem homicídios e latrocínios.

Em agosto, foram registradas 22 vítimas, uma alta de 46,7% em relação ao mesmo mês de 2025, quando foram contabilizadas 15 mortes.

No acumulado de janeiro a agosto, o total passou de 183 mortes, em 2025, para 190 neste ano, um aumento de 3,8%.

O Vale do Paraíba registrou 182 casos de roubos em agosto de 2026. O número representa uma queda de 4,2% em relação ao mesmo mês do ano passado, quando a região teve 190 casos de roubo.

No acumulado do ano, são 1.526 registros de roubo no Vale do Paraíba. O número é menor do que no mesmo período do ano passado, quando a região teve 1.859. A queda é de 17,9%.

Já quanto aos furtos, a região registrou 1.040 casos em agosto de 2026. No mesmo mês de 2025 foram 1.703 casos. Uma diminuição de 38,9%.

No acumulado do ano, são 12.850 casos de furto registrados no Vale do Paraíba. Entre janeiro e agosto de 2025, foram 14.291, uma queda de 10%.Veja mais notícias do Vale do Paraíba e região bragantina.

articles.title: Mangaluru-Goa Vande Bharat to be extended till Bengaluru soon
articles.summary: Railway Ministry to extend Mangaluru–Madgaon Vande Bharat to Bengaluru (Yeshwantpur), cutting travel time; new numbers 26655/26656, date pending.
articles.body: BENGALURU: Railway ministry will soon extend Mangaluru-Madgaon Vande Bharat Express to Bengaluru, meeting two long-standing demands from rail users for premium train services connecting Karnataka’s capital with Mangaluru and Goa.TOI has learnt that railway minister Ashwini Vaishnaw wrote to two MPs from Karnataka, Brijesh Chowta and Vishweshwar Hegde Kageri, earlier this month, communicating the decision to extend the train route.Currently, 20646/20645 Mangaluru Central–Madgaon Vande Bharat Express runs six days a week, with no service Thursdays. According to its timetable, the train takes a little less than six hours to complete a single-direction journey.Proposals to operate Vande Bharat between Bengaluru and Goa were first initiated by South Western Railway (SWR), Konkan Railway Corporation Limited (KRCL) and Southern Railway (SR), in Feb. They suggested the train originate from Yeshwantpur in Bengaluru at 6:05am and reach Madgaon in Goa by 7:15pm, taking 13 hours. Currently, trains between Bengaluru and Goa take around 15 hours.Vaishnaw said the extension will make the train terminate at Yeshwantpur Junction, traversing through Kabaka Puttur and Subrahmanya Road stations. It will become the first self-propelled train to travel along the 55-km ghats section between Sakleshpur and Subrahmanya Road after it was electrified in late 2025.Though the proposal initially suggested a bypass without entering Mangaluru Central station, the plan has now been changed. For Bengaluru-Mangaluru route, two trial runs using a 16-car rake were conducted in Sept, and the train took less than seven hours to complete the journey.The number of commercial stops in the final timetable will determine the total running time. While timings are yet to be finalised, the train will run with entirely new numbers, 26655/26656 in both directions. It will also be renamed Yeshwantpur-Madgaon Vande Bharat Express. articles.title: Aposentada cita pânico ao receber conta de água de quase meio milhão | G1
articles.standfirst: Eliana Aparecida Lopes, de Piracicaba (SP), diz que a fatura costuma variar entre R$ 100 e R$ 150. Serviço Municipal de Água e Esgoto reconheceu erro.
articles.summary: Eliana Aparecida Lopes, de Piracicaba (SP), diz que a fatura costuma variar entre R$ 100 e R$ 150.
articles.body:
A aposentada Eliana Aparecida Lopes, de Piracicaba (SP), destacou o susto que passou ao receber uma conta de água residencial no valor de R$ 470.762,59 .

O Serviço Municipal de Água e Esgoto (Semae) da cidade reconheceu o erro na conta e alegou que ele foi causado por uma falha no hidrômetro.

"[Uma surpresa] Muito grande. Eu estava de manhã tentando entrar no aplicativo do Semae e não estava conseguindo, porque eles trocaram meu registro, e eu estava com medo, eu estava meio ansiosa para vir essa conta porque, toda vez que mexem, dá algum erro. Quando eu olho na caixinha do correio e veja essa conta, fiquei muito assustada", afirmou a aposentada.

A aposentada Eliana Aparecida Lopes destacou o susto com a conta no valor de mais de R$ 470 mil — Foto: Edijan Del Santo/EPTV

Eliana mora com o marido em uma residência no bairro Jardim Abaeté. Segundo ela, a fatura de água, normalmente, varia entre R$ 100 e R$ 150 . No entanto, a conta com vencimento em outubro veio com o valor de quase meio milhão de reais.

A aposentada ressaltou que a indignação aumenta com o risco de a situação acontecer com moradores em condições mais vulneráveis.

"O que mais me deixa indignada é se é uma pessoa sem instrução, sem cuidado, sem ter como se locomover, a gente tem de tudo, as pessoas às vezes não tem condições de ir até o Semae, até a empresa para resolver. O próprio sistema tinha que ter um alerta. Isso não pode acontecer. É um absurdo."

Moradora de Piracicaba (SP) recebeu conta de água residencial no valor de R$ 470.762,59 — Foto: Reprodução/EPTV

O Semae reconheceu que o valor da fatura foi incorreto e motivado por uma falha no hidrômetro da residência

"Em agosto, houve a substituição do hidrômetro da unidade, mas o equipamento apresentou falha, ocasionando a inversão da medição e, consequentemente, a cobrança incorreta", diz o Semae.

De acordo com a autarquia, o problema foi corrigido nesta segunda-feira (28), e a cobrança acabou sendo reajustada para o valor mínimo.

"Na manhã de ontem, 28/09, o hidrômetro foi regularizado e o Semae concluiu todos os ajustes necessários. A cobrança foi corrigida para o valor mínimo de R$ 70,51, com vencimento em 15 de outubro. A usuária receberá uma nova fatura em casa, com os valores devidamente corrigidos", complementou.

Serviço Municipal de Água e Esgoto (Semae) de Piracicaba reconheceu que falha em hidrômetro moticou conta de quase meio milhão de reais — Foto: Edijan Del Santo/EPTV

articles.standfirst: Apostas podem ser feitas até as 20h em lotéricas ou pela internet.
articles.summary: Apostas podem ser feitas até as 20h em lotéricas ou pela internet.
articles.body:
O concurso 3.065 da Mega-Sena pode pagar um prêmio de R$ 75 milhões para os apostadores que acertarem as seis dezenas. O sorteio ocorre às 21h desta quinta-feira (1º), em São Paulo.

No concurso do última terça-feira (29), nenhuma aposta acertou a faixa principal e o valor acumulou.

O g1 transmite todos os sorteios das Loterias Caixa, ao vivo . A transmissão começa momentos antes de cada dia de concursos, no site e no canal do g1 no YouTube .

A aposta mínima para a Mega-Sena custa R$ 6 e pode ser realizada também pela internet – saiba como fazer a sua aposta online .

Volante da Mega-Sena — Foto: Ana Marin/g1

As apostas podem ser realizadas até as 20h (horário de Brasília) em qualquer lotérica do país ou por meio do site e aplicativo Loterias Caixa, disponíveis em smartphones, computadores e outros dispositivos.

Já os bolões digitais poderão ser comprados até as 20h30, exclusivamente pelo portal Loterias Online e pelo aplicativo.

Ainda segundo a Caixa, para os sorteios realizados aos domingos as apostas simples podem ser efetuadas até as 22h de sábado por meio das unidades lotéricas, pelo Portal Loterias Caixa e do aplicativo Loterias Caixa.

A comercialização dos Bolões Caixa nos canais eletrônicos, nesse caso, acontece até às 10h45 do domingo, quinze minutos antes da realização dos sorteios.

O pagamento da aposta online pode ser realizado via PIX, cartão de crédito ou pelo internet banking, para correntistas da Caixa. É preciso ter 18 anos ou mais para participar.

A probabilidade de vencer em cada concurso varia de acordo com o número de dezenas jogadas e do tipo de aposta realizada. Para um jogo simples, com apenas seis dezenas, que custa R$ 6, a probabilidade de ganhar o prêmio milionário é de 1 em 50.063.860, segundo a Caixa.

Já para uma aposta com 20 dezenas (limite máximo), com o preço de R$ 232.560,00, a probabilidade de acertar o prêmio é de 1 em 1.292, ainda de acordo com a instituição.

articles.title: Quem são os quatro heróis que impediram a queda de avião após atentado com faca | G1
articles.standfirst: Passageiro entrou na cabine e assumiu os controles após confronto entre pilotos; comandante ferido abriu a porta e outros dois pilotos fizeram o pouso na Arábia Saudita
articles.summary: Passageiro entrou na cabine e assumiu os controles após confronto entre pilotos; comandante ferido abriu a porta e outros dois pilotos fizeram o pouso na Arábia Saudita
articles.body:
O ataque a faca do copiloto do voo da FlyDubai contra o piloto quase terminou em tragédia na quarta-feira (30). O avião perdeu o controle e despencou mais de 4 mil metros em cerca de 30 segundos , e só não caiu matando os 180 passageiros devido à ação de quatro personagens.

Segundo o primeiro-ministro israelense, Benjamin Netanyahu , a aeronave chegou a "entrar em parafuso e começar a mergulhar". O piloto estava ferido e coberto de sangue, mas ainda conseguiu abrir a porta da cabine de comando. Passageiros então entraram no cockpit e um deles ajudou a conter o copiloto e impedir a queda.

Dois outros pilotos da FlyDubai que viajavam como passageiros assumiram então o controle da aeronave e fizeram o pouso de emergência em Tabuk, na Arábia Saudita .

Netanyahu afirmou que a atuação das pessoas a bordo evitou que o atentado se concretizasse. “Eles salvaram muitas vidas. Evitaram uma grande tragédia”, disse.

Veja quem foram os envolvidos na sequência que permitiu recuperar o controle do avião.

Smit Machchhar foi esfaqueado várias vezes pelo seu copiloto e, mesmo assim, pode abrir a porta da cabine para que a tripulação pudesse salvar o voo. — Foto: Reprodução: LinkedIn / X

Primeiro alvo do ataque, o piloto indiano Smit Machchhar levou várias facadas de seu colega omani. Mesmo ferido, ele conseguiu reagir e alertar as pessoas a bordo sobre o ataque. Passegeiros relataram que conseguiram ouvir os gritos vindos de dentro do cockpit.

Segundo Doron Spielman, porta-voz do gabinete de Netanyahu, o piloto usou seus últimos momentos de energia para liberar a porta da cabine - que só pode ser aberta por dentro.

Imagens feitas depois do incidente mostram Machchhar coberto de sangue e sendo retirado da cabine com uma máscara de oxigênio. Ele foi levado a um hospital na Arábia Saudita.

O estado de saúde do piloto estava estável até a última atualização desta reportagem.

Homem que ajudou a impedir tragédia em avião para Israel foi recebido como herói por Netanyahu — Foto: Reuters

Depois que Machchhar conseguiu abrir a porta da cabine, passageiros correram para ajudar. Entre eles estava o israelense Yaniv Hayun .

Segundo seu próprio relato, Yaniv afirmou que puxou os comandos para cima e conseguiu interromper a queda brusca do avião. Ele também disse que já havia assistido ao programa de televisão "Air Crash Investigation", sobre acidentes aéreos, e que a experiência contribuiu para sua reação durante o episódio.

A sequência exata dessa intervenção ainda não foi esclarecida pelas autoridades.

Ao desembarcar no aeroporto de Ben Gurion, Yaniv Hayun, foi recebido como herói pelo primeiro-ministro israelense. Ao premiê, ele disse ter entrado na cabine ao perceber o confronto entre os dois pilotos.

"É simplesmente inacreditável o que você fez, sabe? Simplesmente inacreditável. Você não apenas salvou todos a bordo do avião. Você não sabe o que poderia ter acontecido com ele. Nós não sabemos o que teria acontecido", disse-lhe Netanyahu.

Depois que passageiros conseguiram conter o copiloto, dois outros pilotos da FlyDubai assumiram o comando da aeronave.

Eles estavam de folga e viajavam como passageiros no mesmo voo até Israel, onde iriam assumir o turno no lugar dos pilotos em serviço. Os dois conseguiram estabilizar o Boeing 737 e conduzi-lo até Tabuk, no noroeste da Arábia Saudita.

A companhia aérea afirmou que o avião foi controlado com sucesso pela tripulação que estava a bordo e que a aeronave conseguiu pousar em segurança.

Os nomes dos dois pilotos ainda não haviam sido divulgados até a publicação desta reportagem.

Neste episódio, Natuza Nery recebe Felipe Nunes para analisar muitos desses movimentos captados nas pesquisas de opinião. O cientista político explica por que o medo é o sentimento que mais mobiliza os eleitores e avalia os impactos do Caso Master, da crise do STF e da polêmica envolvendo N. S. articles.title: Celebrity Traitors: What you need to know ahead of the first show
articles.summary: Maya Jama, Michael Sheen and Bella Ramsey are among this year's celebrities taking part in the show.
articles.body:
The Celebrity Traitors is back for a second series, and viewers will see the likes of Michael Sheen, Jerry Hall, Richard E Grant and Amol Rajan at the round table along with Bella Ramsey, Leigh-Anne Pinnock, Maya Jama and King Kenny.

There are 21 celebrities taking part in total - two more than last year - and there will be an extra episode after the huge popularity of last year's series.

The extended 75-minute debut episode starts at 20:00 BST on Thursday, with Claudia Winkleman again hosting the murderous game.

Viewers can expect some fresh ideas, and executive producer Sarah Fay said they "always want to push the envelope" with the show's elaborate tasks.

"We're always trying to evolve existing ideas to bring them into a new life or coming up with different cultural references," she told the show's press launch.

The celebrities will be playing for a £100,000 cash prize for charity.

The final amount will depend on how well they perform in the tasks, regardless of any possible tensions over who is a faithful and who is a traitor.

This year's contestants are a mixture of famous faces from TV, film, radio and YouTube:

Maya Jama – broadcaster and entrepreneur

Professor Hannah Fry– broadcaster and mathematician

Celebrity Traitors 2 cast: Who are this year's 'big dogs' and dark horses?

In the show's trailer , they are seen arriving in a church, smiling as they greet each other, but looking nervous.

They later travel to the castle in a fleet of black cars, before Winkleman chooses her traitors while everyone wears their blindfolds.

They then take part in their first mission in a lake in wetsuits, ending with Winkleman saying ominously: "Fame won't save them."

Speaking at the press launch, Winkleman said she is totally focused on the celebrities while she's in the castle, and is glued to the monitors showing footage of them throughout the day.

"All of them were tremendous, and when we do any series I have this room with the monitors. I'm like a weirdo just applying fake tan, watching," she said.

The presenter added that even when she's told to go home, she tells the producers "I am not leaving", joking that she got barely any sleep.

Ed Gamble, host of BBC Two spin-off show Uncloaked, added that he watched "hours of footage a day" as well.

"So when they're eating breakfast, I'm eating breakfast watching them eat breakfast. It's actually quite sad... I'm normally sat there in my pyjamas eating cereal, watching them eat cereal," he told BBC News.

Viewers can also look forward to more of Winkleman's eclectic wardrobe choices.

"I like the fact that it is 'human crow meets golf caddy meets the Artful Dodger'. We're pretty happy with it," she joked about this year's outfits.

The celebrities have also been speaking about the show before its launch , with comedian and presenter Romesh Ranganathan saying that despite being best friends with fellow comic Rob Beckett, he would have no problem stabbing him in the back.

"I mean, he's just as easily going to be on my side as he is going to twist the knife in my back given the opportunity," he said.

The show's other comics include Joe Lycett, James Acaster and Joanne McNally.

"I think we're going to be the first ones under the magnifying glass being looked at," Acaster said over suspicions one will be a traitor.

Comedian Alan Carr won the first series of Celebrity Traitors, which was the most watched TV programme of 2025 in the UK, watched by 15 million people.

The Last of Us and Game of Thrones star Bella Ramsey already has experience of playing similar games at drama clubs and at home, which is why they joined the show.

"I've been playing a version of The Traitors since I was 10 years old," they said.

Mathematician Hannah Fry, who called herself "toxically competitive", added she has already looked for "statistical patterns" in the data for previous games; while Little Mix singer Leigh-Anne Pinnock said she took advice from singer Cat Burns, who reached the final as a traitor last year.

"She had good advice. She said it might get intense around that round table – but remember, it's just a game," Pinnock said.

The show is also something of a love letter to the Scottish Highlands, where it is filmed, with sweeping drone shots of the scenery and Ardross Castle in Inverness, where the celebrities meet, eat and of course sit at the round table.

"It's breathtaking," Winkleman told the press, adding that she and her family were returning to the Highlands for a holiday.

"My husband was like, 'You're already there quite a lot, what's the matter with you?'" she said.

"It's the most beautiful place I've ever been in the world, is the truth."

After she recently chose to end her recent BBC One chat show , Winkleman is back on familiar ground with Celebrity Traitors.

BBC News asked if she would ever want to try being a contestant on the show, perhaps in the US or Australian versions.

"No, I'm too thick," she said in typical self-deprecating style.

"I mustn't play it in public. I must not.

"I'm just being honest - it's a privilege to play that game and to be at the round table, but I think I would just be too awful at it."

The Celebrity Traitors series two begins on Thursday 1 October at 20:00 BST on BBC One and iPlayer . The series will air two nights a week, on Thursday and Friday evenings.

articles.title: BBC paying to air shows like Suits and Schitt's Creek is illogical, MPs say
articles.summary: The issue is one of several raised by an influential committee as debate about the BBC's future continues.
articles.body:
The BBC should not pay "over the odds" for the rights to overseas hits such as Suits and Schitt's Creek, an influential group of MPs has said.

It is one of several issues raised in a wide-ranging report about the BBC's funding and future, published by the House of Commons' cross-party culture and media committee.

Although the BBC produces a lot of its own programmes, the corporation buys some international shows for its TV channels and iPlayer streaming platform.

The MPs' report said the BBC could "spend more wisely when competing for programming". Overall, the BBC brings "immeasurable benefits" to society but needs reform of the TV licence fee to avoid a fate of "managed decline", they said.

Committee chair Dame Caroline Dinenage said the report comes at "a pivotal moment for the BBC", which is grappling with changing media habits, declining income and negotiations with the government over how it is paid for.

Dame Caroline said the government "must ensure the BBC has a universal and sustainable source of funding".

But, she added, the BBC "can play its part by sweating its assets and boxing clever for the licence payer by ending illogical practices such as outbidding commercial rivals for overseas hits such as Suits, Schitt's Creek and Scooby Doo".

The rights to air all three programmes were bought by the BBC after contracts with other networks or streaming services expired.

"At a time of constrained resources, the BBC should not be paying over the odds for overseas content, particularly when it's a bidding war against commercial UK broadcasters," the committee said.

The MPs added that they "did not believe that this provides value for money for the licence fee payer".

The BBC said it spends less than 5% of its content budget on acquiring shows, less than other broadcasters, and they are a cost-effective way of delivering high-quality content to audiences who go on to discover homegrown programming.

The committee's report has been published as the government considers its options for the next BBC Royal Charter, which will set out how the broadcaster will be governed, regulated and funded from 2028 onwards.

Dame Caroline said: "For all its faults, the BBC drives our creative economy, supports our democracy through media sovereignty, and delivers world-class entertainment and moments that bring us together.

"Like a much-loved family member, we may criticise and grumble about the BBC but we would miss it enormously if it were no longer here for us."

The committee said there were "considerable challenges" for the BBC and warned that the current TV licence fee is "outdated and no longer fit for purpose".

Currently, about 94% of individuals use the BBC each month but only 80% of households pay for a TV licence, the MPs noted.

"The licence fee should be reformed so it is no longer linked to the consumption of live TV or to a particular device, such as a television set," the committee said.

"This should be an easier sell to licence fee payers if expanding the base is paired with a drop in the individual cost."

The BBC's director-general Matt Brittin has previously described the current licence fee model as "a busted flush" and "yesterday's model", and has said the price could be cut if more people pay under an overhauled system.

The committee also suggested the BBC should:

Explore the opportunity for introducing an international TV licence so it can increase its revenue and global audience

Work with independent production companies who own the rights to many of its programmes to ensure more remain on iPlayer

Develop its current premises with facilities that can "harness the potential of new media and support the creator economy"

The committee suggested the government should:

Support the corporation by legislating to put a BBC button on remote controls for smart TVs

Press YouTube to give a certain level of prominence for content made by the BBC and other British public service broadcasters

Take back full funding for the BBC World Service, describing it as "the UK's number one soft power asset"

The committee supported opening up BBC iPlayer to shows from other public service broadcasters such as Channel 4.

Earlier this week, Channel 4 chief executive Priya Dogra said she was open to her network's content being hosted on iPlayer.

The report also called for the end of political appointments to the BBC board, to improve governance and remain trusted by the public.

And the committee recommended that the BBC is given new public purposes relating to innovation and technology and combating misinformation and disinformation.

The BBC welcomed the report, which it said made "some important and interesting recommendations on the future of the BBC".

A BBC spokesperson said: "We have consistently argued that the current funding model is outdated and needs reform, so we welcome the Committee's support for maintaining universal funding while overhauling the licence fee.

"We are also pleased to see their recognition of the vital work of the World Service, with a clear recommendation that responsibility for funding should return fully to Government.

"At a time of huge disruption in the media, the BBC's trust, reach and creative strength remain unparalleled. But we also recognise the need to evolve and move faster towards the future."

The government's Department for Digital, Culture, Media and Sport (DCMS) said it "agrees entirely with the Committee's conclusion that it is in the country's best interests for the next Charter to support an ambitious and innovative BBC, and that the corporation cannot be left to a future of managed decline".

A DCMS spokesperson added: "We will review and consider the committee's recommendations in detail, alongside the views of the public and other stakeholders, to inform decisions for the next Royal Charter."

TV licence fee is 'yesterday's model', new BBC director general says

articles.title: LSU student says she was raped by a football player who is still on the team
articles.summary: “LSU does really protect their athletes, especially their football players,” says the woman, whose claims are being investigated by the local district attorney.
articles.body: A Louisiana State University student who claims a school football player raped her last year is speaking out about how the school handled her report and the lack of guidance she said she received throughout the process. Kendall Danielle Francis talked on TikTok about the monthslong Title IX investigation that played out after she reported the October rape to the school. Two days into the current semester, she said, she received an email while she was in class to notify her that the student, who had been suspended for two semesters, had his punishment modified upon appeal to four semesters’ probation. He would remain on campus and could continue to play football, she said. “Now I am just trying to speak on my story, because LSU does really protect their athletes, especially their football players,” Francis, who was 18 at the time of the alleged incident, said in the Sept. 14 social media post. As a result of the student’s remaining on campus, Francis said, she moved her classes online. Francis wasn’t aware that filing the Title IX complaint was a separate process from filing criminal charges, a spokesperson for Francis said Wednesday. “When she filed for Title IX, they [the university] did not tell her she could also contact the police and have them launch a criminal investigation,” a spokesperson said. “She just assumed LSU would do the criminal investigation.” Francis’ post, however, caught the attention of East Baton Rouge Parish District Attorney Hillar Moore, whose office announced it was launching a criminal investigation. He has requested “all reports, interviews, evidence, and other relevant records” from LSU, the university police and the Baton Rouge Police Department, as well as the coroner’s office, which handles the evidence collection from sexual assault victims. “This is now an open criminal investigation,” Moore said Sept. 22 in a statement on his agency’s Facebook page. Francis’ allegations come as accusations that members of a fraternity gang-raped a female Cornell University student for several hours have renewed questions nationwide about whether universities are doing enough to protect students from sexual assault. LSU President Wade Rousse said in a statement that the university is cooperating with investigators. “Let me assure everyone that this incident has been handled professionally and that LSU has strictly followed our policies, procedures and best practices, including the Title IX process, to guide our actions to date,” Rousse said. Title IX is a federal law that requires all universities that receive federal funds to put safeguards in place to protect students from sexual predators. Francis didn’t respond to several reach-outs from NBC News to discuss her online allegations or share the findings of the Title IX investigation. In her TikTok video, Francis said she was assaulted at around 4:30 a.m. Oct. 18 “by a football player at LSU.” “That day basically changed my life,” she said, adding that she “developed pretty severe anxiety” and that after an official diagnosis she began taking medication to manage it. Francis said that she was taken to the hospital, where she had “a rape kit done,” but that she didn’t initially press charges. “However, I did go through the Title IX process here at LSU, which took a really, really long time,” she said. Francis said she returned to school assuming the football player was suspended and under investigation by the police. She said she was in a class when she was notified via email that the alleged attacker was still “accountable” for the rape and would be on probation and allowed to attend classes on campus and play football. “I was under the impression that because LSU found him responsible that LSU would do their part, that criminal charges, you know, would be pursued,” Francis said in an interview last week with WAFB-TV of Baton Rouge. Universities are generally not required to automatically alert the police when a Title IX sexual assault or rape investigation is underway, especially if the survivor requests confidentiality or chooses not to involve law enforcement. Francis said in a second TikTok post that she reported the alleged rape this month to LSU police in an attempt to press charges. NBC News has reached out to the agency to confirm that, but so far there has been no response. The Baton Rouge-based newspaper The Advocate reported that it had obtained the Title IX documents from the case and that they confirm Francis’ assertion that the football player was found responsible for the rape. Those documents, according to the newspaper, also confirm that his punishment was reduced on appeal from a two-semester suspension to four semesters of probation. Some of the sexual activity between Francis and the football player was consensual, according to those documents as reported by The Advocate. Still, the football player admitted that he didn’t specifically ask for Francis’ consent before they had intercourse “and did not stop when he later asked and she was silent,” according to the Title IX documents. Meg Casper Sunstrom, an LSU spokesperson, didn’t confirm the outcome of the Title IX proceedings or the discipline that was handed down to the student. Nor did she respond to questions about whether the football player was at LSU and playing for the team. “Since there was no criminal complaint filed by the victim, LSU appropriately turned the issue over to our Title IX office as mandated by law,” Sunstrom said in an email. But she noted that the football player did “self-report” an incident involving his accuser with the LSU Police Department. Dated Oct. 18, 2025, the report, obtained from LSU via a public records request, said the 19-year-old football player was at the school’s football facility when he called police “due to concerns about potential accusations from the other party.” The report gave no indication what those potential accusations were. The incident report says the football player told police that Francis had told him she was mentally unwell and had “thoughts of suicidal ideation.” The responding officer noted in the report that police had been in touch with Francis four days earlier, on Oct. 14, “regarding a similar incident.” An officer determined that Francis posed no danger to herself and “seemed to be commenting out of spite.” This time, the report says, when police went to Francis’ on-campus residence, “it was evident that Francis’s mental state was unstable.” The report doesn’t detail the basis for that conclusion. “She agreed to go to the hospital for further evaluation, and I transported her to Baton Rouge General Hospital for assessment,” the responding officer wrote in his report. Francis said in her TikTok post that she dreads the possibility of running into her alleged attacker on campus. “So that made my anxiety really, really bad, because I don’t want to face this person,” she said. “I really just wanted to bring awareness upon this situation, because I’m just dealing with a lot right now, and I think that this story needs to be heard.”

articles.title: 'Nobody Wants This': Consulting rabbi calls out star's 'ignorant' take on 'genocide' in Gaza
articles.summary: Rabbi Steve Leder, a former consulting advisor on Netflix's "Nobody Wants This," called star Adam Brody's Gaza genocide claim "ignorant" and his tone "disgusting."
articles.body: Rabbi Steve Leder, a technical advisor behind Netflix's "Nobody Wants This," called out the series star Adam Brody on Tuesday for saying he believes Israel is committing "genocide" in Gaza. "Hi Adam, you might not remember me. My name is Rabbi Steve Leder, and I was the technical advisor for Season 1 of 'Nobody Wants This,'" Leder began in an Instagram video to the actor. "My job was to make sure that your character was authentic and that everything in Season 1 about Judaism was authentic." Leder criticized Brody and called his comments "ignorant," arguing that Brody had mischaracterized the situation in Gaza and treated the issue flippantly. BILL MAHER RIPS MACKLEMORE'S GAZA STANCE, SAYS CELEBRITY 'MORAL CONFUSION' IS FUELING ANTISEMITISM "Your pronouncement the other day about a ‘genocide in Gaza’ was truly shocking," Leder said. "Not only because of your misuse and mischaracterization of your use of the word genocide — there is no genocide in Gaza, there are genocides in other countries happening, but you failed to mention any of them. "You, by your own admission, are a relatively ignorant Jew, and your ignorance really showed the other day. "If you’re going to use a word like ‘genocide,’ you ought to know what it means," he added. "And, by the way, being so flippant about a word like ‘genocide’ — ‘Hey, put me down for genocide,’ like you’re asking for a table for two at Craig’s — is disgusting. Here’s some more technical advice: If you know nothing about something, you should say nothing about it." Brody, who plays a rabbi in the series, recently suggested in an interview with GQ magazine that Israel is committing "genocide" in Gaza. "Put me down as thinking it's a genocide," Brody said. "Put me down as wanting a free Palestine. It's awful that it's taken so much death and misery, but it does feel like it's reaching a breaking point that it should have a while ago. I'm hopeful that another administration can really do some good and correct some of these policies that are helping that situation be as awful as it is." Fox News Digital reached out to Brody's representatives for comment but did not immediately receive a response. RABBINIC GROUP ACCUSES JEWISH ENTERTAINERS OF 'WHITEWASHING ANTISEMITISM' IN MARK RUFFALO DEFENSE In a comment to Fox News Digital, Rabbi Yaakov Menken, executive vice president of the Coalition for Jewish Values, also called out Brody as "ignorant" for calling Israel's actions in Gaza "genocide." "One of the hallmarks of antisemitism is to irrationally regard Jews as a threat. While Hamas was holding, torturing, raping and murdering hostages, only a bigot would call the effort to free those hostages ‘genocide.’ An ignorant Jew is no less likely than anyone else to fall prey to hateful indoctrination," Menken said. "As even photographer Motaz Azaiza now admits, Hamas could have ended the conflict in Gaza at any moment, simply by releasing the hostages," he added. "In no genocide in history have the victims controlled the off switch. On roughly a daily basis, a prominent Jewish leftist goes on X (formerly Twitter) to say ‘As a Jew’ and then follow it by expressing antisemitic nonsense." Just today, Israeli passengers narrowly escaped death from what is being called an attempted terrorist attack on a flight from Dubai to Tel Aviv. That's the reality Israelis and Jews live with every day," the organization said.

articles.title: Son who used AI to help save mum's life hopes case can help other Parkinson's patients
articles.summary: Doctors say clinical trials are needed to understand more after Ed Patrick identified a potential side effect of a Parkinson's drug.
articles.body:
An NHS doctor who says he saved his mum's life with the help of AI hopes what he learned can help others with Parkinson's Disease complications.

Ed Patrick, an anaesthetist from Oxfordshire, was at his mother's bedside in hospital ready to say his goodbyes after she began suffering serious and continuous seizures.

Using AI to scour recent medical journal articles, he said he identified a vitamin deficiency linked to her Parkinson's medication as a possible cause, and staff then gave her a vitamin dose that appeared to stop the seizures.

Doctors say clinical trials are needed to understand more - and warn against patients making changes to their own medication without medical advice.

Charity Parkinson's UK welcomed the prospect of more research trials in light of this case and said it could "transform care" for some others with Parkinson's.

In May this year Patrick said hospital staff called to say his mother, Ann, was close to death, after she had been deteriorating over several months.

"She was taken to hospital with non-stop fits and convulsions," he told BBC Radio 2's Jeremy Vine Show.

"I got a phone call from the hospital's medical registrar who told me they'd tried all the anti-seizure medications and they weren't working. 'Sorry, she's dying', the registrar told me. 'Do I have time to make it?', I said. 'Yes, but you've got to leave now' was her reply."

When he got to the hospital in Nottinghamshire, Patrick said his mother was "totally unconscious", suffering continuous fits and going into kidney failure.

He said he used Google's Gemini AI tool to summarise recent medical journal articles relevant to his mum's condition and symptoms, and then relayed it to the neurology consultant.

"I told him what I'd discovered - that the seizures were almost certainly a rare side effect of a vitamin B6 deficiency, possibly caused by her long-term carbidopa-levodopa dopamine use, which was being used to treat her Parkinson's," he said. Carbidopa-levodopa is a combination drug commonly used to boost dopamine levels in Parkinson's patients.

Medical staff agreed to give Ann an intravenous supplement of vitamin B6, which appeared to stop her seizures.

"She hasn't had a seizure since," he said. "The next day the family and medics were all ecstatic. The neurologist was high-fiving me."

The consultant neurologist in question, Dr Bruno Gran from Nottingham University Hospitals, said: "As an anaesthetist, Ed has a strong understanding of clinical pharmacology and his reasoning was sound.

"What we did not anticipate was the speed and magnitude of the response. Within minutes of administering vitamin B6, Ann's seizure activity stopped.

"We are now working to raise awareness of this potential issue, beginning with changes to practice within our own team. Although Parkinson's affects millions of people worldwide, only 14 similar cases have ever been reported. But if the insights gained from this case can help clinicians identify and prevent similar situations in the future, that would be a significant and positive outcome."

Ann has since made a full recovery from the seizures and Patrick said her day-to-day cognitive Parkinson's symptoms have dramatically improved.

"It's like we've got mum back", said Patrick. "It feels like we found a silver bullet. She's sharp as a tack.

"She's been given a really good quality of life from a solution we never even knew was there. Cognitively, it's like she's gone back in time five to 10 years."

Parkinson's is a progressive disorder that affects the brain, nervous system, and muscle control. About 166,000 people in the UK live with the condition, according to Parkinson's UK.

Patrick believes B6 vitamins could help other Parkinson's patients, both in emergency settings, but also in some cases of long-term cognitive deterioration.

"I think this has potentially wide-reaching ramifications for others. I know that mum's medical team has presented her case to colleagues and that's led to changes in practice in the region. They're looking at where B6 supplementation might be appropriate."

Existing clinical evidence on the link between B6 deficiency in Parkinson's patients and any potential impact it can have is still limited. Experts told the BBC that the link is not known about by the majority of NHS staff in the UK.

But earlier this year, the US Food and Drug Administration put out a memo saying that particular drugs used to treat Parkinson's should carry a warning about potential links to B6 deficiency.

Dr Graham Johnson, a consultant in emergency medicine who co-leads the Research in Emergency Medicine in Derby group and has been discussing the case with Patrick, said: "Sometimes the best research ideas come from patients' stories, and experts in Parkinson's may now be able to use this case to build a wider evidence base through studies and clinical trials."

The chief executive of Parkinson's UK, Caroline Rassell, said they "support the move towards more research trials into vitamin B6 deficiency and Parkinson's".

"It's needed to help us understand the connections. The findings and recommendations could transform care for people with Parkinson's."

Rassell and other medics told the BBC that patients living with Parkinson's should treat this information with caution.

"This family's experience will definitely raise awareness of the link between vitamin B6 and Parkinson's medications," said Rassell.

"However, never make changes to medications or supplements before taking medical advice," she said, and encouraged anyone concerned to speak with their medical team or call the Parkinson's UK helpline.

Consultant neurologist Prof Tom Foltynie, who specialises in Parkinson's at University College London Hospitals NHS Trust, said: "Patients should bear in mind that excessively high doses of vitamin B6 can also cause problems, so anyone who is concerned about their B6 levels should request a blood test to check their levels before seeking B6 supplements.

"While there's fledgling awareness of this link between low B6 and potential risks of negative outcomes, is hasn't penetrated enough so that B6 is prescribed for more than a trivial amount of Parkinson's patients.

"Having a modest lowering of these vitamin levels probably doesn't have consequences for the vast majority of people. But hearing this story emphasises that this is potentially very important, and it will ring bells for a great number of people who work with Parkinson's patients, to more regularly check levels of B vitamins, and supplement if needed."

Not long after recovering from the seizures, Ann was fit enough to hold Patrick's baby - her youngest granddaughter - and read her a story from the hospital bed.

"She's absolutely glorious," said Ann. "Beautiful. And we get to see her quite a lot. I'm very very grateful to Edward and the rest of the family. It seems such a small thing - that a 'bit of a vitamin' could make a difference between life and death."

articles.title: California bans child marriage, a practice still legal in 32 US states
articles.summary: Gov Gavin Newsom called it a "long overdue measure to protect young Californians".
articles.body:
California has officially banned child marriage, with Governor Gavin Newsom signing legislation to end the practice that is still legal in 32 US states.

The new law, which will come into effect on 1 January, states people must be 18 to get married in the Golden State.

Newsom called it a "long overdue measure to protect young Californians and minors". He signed the bill into law with Courtney Stodden, whose parents allowed her to marry a 50-year-old Hollywood actor when she was just 16.

Stodden, who has been advocating to end the practice, called the change a "victory" and said survivors of child marriage should "never have been expected to carry this burden".

Stodden said she would "keep fighting until children are protected from marriage in all 50 states".

She was married to actor Doug Hutchison - known for roles in The Green Mile, A Time to Kill and I Am Sam - in 2011, spurring headlines internationally over the controversy and appearances on several reality programmes in the US, including the VH1 series Couples Therapy.

Other survivors of child marriage also applauded the new law.

"California has sent a clear message to the world today," Brittany Bee, a former child bride, told the BBC. "A message of hope for all children that they may be free from systemic violence. That they may choose their own path."

Bee told the BBC she was wed at the age of 17 to escape an abusive home - only to then be allegedly abused by her adult husband.

"I was just going from one prison to another," she explained. "People have the audacity to tell me that I made a choice - kids, they can't consent."

Bee and other child marriage survivors have been working for years to have child marriages banned in California and across the United States.

About a decade ago, the practice was still allowed across all US state but more and more states have been altering laws. California is the 18th to ban it since 2018.

In the state, there had been no legal age to wed, allowing children to get married as long as their parents consent and a judge signs off on the nuptials.

There was also no mechanism for people under 18 to get divorced and many girls say they were trapped in abusive and predatory relationships.

Unchained At Last, an advocacy group fighting to end child marriage across the US, said about 9,000 girls were wed each year in California and that almost all child marriages involved girls to adult men.

Advocates say that many in the US don't even know that child marriage is legal in so many US states, nor that is has led to allegations of abuse.

Sara Tasneem, who says she was forced to marry a man nearly twice her age when she was 15 years old, told the BBC that it felt "surreal" to finally have the state recognise that child marriage should be banned. She says she started lobbying for this herself in 2017.

She was introduced to her husband the morning of their arranged marriage.

"I was forced to be his wife and that day, my entire life changed," she told the BBC. She became a mother the following year, at the age of 16, and dropped out of school.

"To have seen the arc of this bill come to fruition has been a marathon," Tasneem said. "I'm just grateful that kids cannot get married after January 1, 2027 in California."

articles.title: How the new prison release scheme will work - and how many inmates will be set free
articles.summary: Hundreds of eligible offenders will leave jails in England and Wales on 1 October, under the government's early prison release plan.
articles.body:
About 700 eligible offenders will leave jails in England and Wales on 1 October while some 2,550 are due to be released by the end of the year, under the government's early prison release plan.

So why are so many people being let out of jail earlier than expected and how have they been chosen?

Quite simply, prisons are almost full - and not for the first time.

As of last Friday, there were 87,499 people in 120 jails across England and Wales - with around 1,500 available beds. At this rate, there would be no spare cells by Christmas.

The early release scheme was developed because of a crisis the Labour government inherited when it came to power in July 2024.

Back then, prisons were rapidly running out of cells because courts were jailing more criminals than the number being released - part of a 30-year trend.

The outgoing government had also failed to build the prisons it had promised.

By the summer of 2024 there were virtually no free cells left, so the Ministry of Justice ran an emergency scheme, releasing some offenders after serving 40% of their sentence, rather than 50% - when most fixed-term prisoners are eligible for release.

From Thursday a permanent scheme passed by Parliament comes into force.

Which prisoners are being released and when?

The scheme applies to roughly 70,000 offenders. If they had expected to serve half their term in jail and half in the community on a licence, the eligible prisoners will now leave at the one-third point.

The first eligible group are those jailed for up to 19 months. From November, it will be offenders serving up to three years and two months. By next June, serious offenders on fixed terms of more than 12 years will become eligible. Many of them will have expected to serve two-thirds of their sentence behind bars. Instead they will be on a community licence after serving half of their time.

The total length of their sentences has not changed - just the date when they become eligible to start serving part of that sentence in the community.

Some 18,000 inmates are completely excluded - including those convicted of murder, manslaughter, a sexual or grooming-related offence, or a driving offence that led to a death. Their earliest release dates remain unchanged.

How many prisoners are expected to be released early?

Roughly 4,500 prisoners are due to be released by next summer. Some 700 will leave jail on the morning of 1 October - if spread equally across all jails that would be around six per prison.

In a typical month, around 4,500 people leave jails - so the first year of the scheme will see an 8% jump in releases.

What happens after prisoners are released?

When someone leaves prison while still serving a sentence, they are released on licence, which means they could be recalled if they break their conditions - this ranges from failing to make a probation appointment or not living at an approved address, through to more serious breaches such as contacting a victim, abandoning a rehabilitation programme or committing a crime.

The new rules, called "Earned Progression", are meant to encourage them to work harder to reform through enhanced monitoring and intensive supervision.

This means more released prisoners will have to wear electronic tags and be subject to other conditions.

If they step out of line, they can be returned to jail immediately.

Probation officers will have to work harder to monitor offenders all around the country. Martin Jones, the independent inspector of the service, has said he is "not fully confident" that the system will be able to cope.

The staff union says officers already have too many cases and the rate at which they are leaving the profession has increased. A report, published days before the start of the October early releases, warned that almost half of offenders were not tagged promptly, despite electronic monitoring being key to success.

The government says the probation service has recruited 1,300 more staff and has also received new AI tools to help it oversee offenders.

How many offenders are recalled to prison?

An offender can be recalled to prison immediately if their probation officer or the Parole Board believes they have broken their licence conditions, if the risk they pose increases, or if they pose a danger to the public.

According to the latest official figures, there were 51,419 licence recalls in the year ending March 2026 - up 28% on the previous year.

Those recalls were slightly lower than the previous three-month period.

Of those 51,419, around one in five was recalled for general "non compliance" and about one in 10 for failing to be in touch with their probation officer. Around 2,900 had committed another offence.

The government hopes - and this is the big bet - that if there is more community rehabilitation, more offenders can be kept out of jail.

Why has the government chosen these prisoners and not others?

The original scheme, which was devised when Sir Keir Starmer was prime minister, would have allowed about 500 more offenders to be released.

Sir Keir's successor Andy Burnham said he would rethink the proposals amid public alarm, lobbying from victims of grooming gangs and anger over the potential early release of two of the men who killed Pc Andrew Harper.

Burnham said if the scheme was scrapped, prisons would become full and the courts would have to stop sentencing new criminals.

The government projects that the prison population will still rise to around 100,000 by 2030. So the £7bn prison-building programme it has promised is crucial - aiming to deliver 14,000 extra cells by then.

Another key element of the plan is the effective scrapping of one-year jail terms. The law now says that judges should normally suspend such terms - meaning the offender won't go to prison unless they commit another crime.

That policy is backed by some long-standing evidence that fewer people re-offend if they receive intensive supervision to sort out their lives, rather than locking them up for short sentences.

We fear for our lives after being told our abusive exes will be freed from jail early

What's behind having to release some prisoners early?

articles.title: UK accuses China of using academics to spy on AI and other tech research
articles.summary: Britain’s MI5 spy agency issued an unprecedented alert on ​Wednesday to warn that a Chinese organization was involved in funding academic research into topics such as AI on behalf ‌of Beijing’s state security service.
articles.body: Britain’s MI5 spy agency issued an unprecedented alert on ​Wednesday to warn that a Chinese organization was involved in funding academic research into topics such as AI on behalf ‌of Beijing’s state security service. In its “Espionage Alert”, MI5 said more than 100 UK-based academics had contributed to projects funded by the China General Technology Research Institute (CGTRI), which had “very strong ties” to the Chinese Ministry of State Security (MSS), Beijing’s civilian intelligence service. “MI5 has identified that the primary purpose of CGTRI is to fund academic research that directly ​improves MSS technical capability for espionage,” the alert said. “UK academics have contributed to CGTRI-funded projects on topics including Artificial Intelligence (AI), cybersecurity, covert ​communications systems and steganography. This activity supports MSS espionage, which poses a threat to UK national security.” Steganography is the ⁠practice of hiding information within messages or objects. The warning, which MI5 said was the first time it had independently published an alert publicly, is ​the latest in a series of accusations concerning Chinese espionage activities, and highlights the tension between British security concerns and the government’s moves to ​build ties with Beijing. China’s embassy in Britain described the allegations as “imaginary and purely fabricated”. “We firmly oppose such baseless allegations and have lodged solemn representations with the UK side,” an embassy spokesperson said in a statement. “We urge the UK intelligence authorities to stop spreading falsehoods and stop undermining educational exchanges and research cooperation between China and the UK.” UK minister vows “robust action” against threats MI5 said many academics and institutions would have engaged in good faith with the CGTRI, which it said was sometimes ​translated as the China Academy of General Technology (CAGT), without knowing of its close ties to the MSS. But it said those who continued to do so would now ‌risk prosecution ⁠under Britain’s National Security Act, which was passed in 2023 to give greater powers to target foreign spying and hostile state activities. Security minister Dan Jarvis said he had written to all university chiefs in Britain to ensure staff ended any relationship with the Chinese organization. “This alert exposes attempts by Chinese intelligence to covertly benefit from the expertise and research of our academics, undermining our national security, and that of our allies,” he said in a ​statement. “International partnerships are vital to ensure ​our universities and research institutes ⁠continue to thrive, but we will take robust action to defend against the threats we face.” Britain’s relationship with China has become increasingly complicated in recent years. On the one hand, the British government has sought better relations with ​Beijing to improve trade ties and approved plans for China to build its latest embassy in Europe in London, but ​it has also ⁠repeatedly warned of Chinese spying efforts and attempts to undermine UK democracy. Last year, Ken McCallum, MI5’s director-general, said Chinese spies posed a daily national security threat, and were creating fake job adverts to try to lure British professionals into handing over information. His agency also issued an alert to British lawmakers last November that Chinese agents were ⁠targeting them ​to collect information and influence their activity by posing as headhunters or companies. In June, security ​agencies from the “Five Eyes” alliance of the US, Britain, Canada, Australia and New Zealand published a warning about Chinese spies aggressively using online job platforms to recruit people with access to ​sensitive information. China’s London embassy said that warning was “entirely fabricated and constitutes malicious slander”.

articles.title: Hasan Piker speaks to UT Austin students after backlash from Texas lawmakers
articles.summary: Hasan Piker took the stage at UT Austin despite bipartisan backlash from Greg Abbott, Ted Cruz and others, drawing a packed venue of cheering students.
articles.body: After much scrutiny, controversial Twitch streamer Hasan Piker spoke to students at the University of Texas in Austin. Sporting a Longhorn orange tie and pin, Piker began the stream in his hotel room and continued it backstage at UT Austin before he finally took the stage. On Sunday, the University Democrats said they were forced to "return tickets to thousands of students," claiming that UT Austin refused to give them a larger space and an off-campus venue decided it would not host the event after "internal discussions." The student group declared it would not cancel the event despite outside pressure to do so. Piker was welcomed into the event Wednesday evening with loud cheers and applause. The venue looked almost entirely filled. He opened his speech with "Hook 'Em Horns," garnering another wave of cheers. The streamer went on to thank the students for attending the event despite the backlash it received. CONTROVERSIAL STREAMER HASAN PIKER'S LECTURE AXED BY UNIVERSITY OF WASHINGTON AMID FREE SPEECH QUESTIONS "There was supposed to be 3,000 people here today. Three thousand. It's a real testament to how much progress can be made in even a state like Texas that the people in the national Democratic Party have left behind," Piker told the crowd. "That's why I wanted to come here today, not just because of the pushback, not in spite of the pushback, but because I know for a fact that there are people who want their voices to be heard." At the top of his speech, Piker addressed allegations he hates the U.S., saying, "I always tell people that if I hated America, I'd be a Republican." He went on to accuse President Donald Trump of "destroying" the country. In his remarks, Piker focused much of his ire on Republicans, Trump, U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement and Israel. The event was hosted by the University Democrats, a student group at UT Austin, and it drew backlash soon after it was announced. Ahead of the event, Texas lawmakers from both sides of the aisle, including Gov. Greg Abbott, Sen. Ted Cruz and Rep. Henry Cuellar condemned Piker's appearance in the Lone Star State. And Piker condemned all of them at the beginning of his remarks at the university. HASAN PIKER DOUBLES DOWN, DEFENDS HIS 'GOD-GIVEN RIGHT' TO SAY HOW MUCH HE HATES AMERICA Cuellar raised concerns on X about Jewish students at UT Austin being made to feel unsafe due to Piker's presence. The Twitch streamer approached their criticism by speaking about the First Amendment and the importance of freedom of speech. However, he argued that those on the left are not given the same freedom as their ideological counterparts on the right. Additionally, Andrew Mahaleris, press secretary for Texas Gov. Greg Abbott, also chimed in, telling Jewish News Syndicate (JNS), "Terrorist sympathizers have no place in Texas." In a statement provided to Fox News Digital Sept. 16, Cruz said the event was a statement about the status of the Democratic Party. "Hasan Piker is an America-hating Marxist who has said that America deserved 9/11 and celebrates political violence against Republicans," Cruz's statement said. "Americans are entitled to free speech, but it is incumbent upon good people to condemn Piker's incitement. Instead, some Democrats are bringing him to college campuses, while almost all other Democrats are conspicuously silent or worse. It says everything about the state of their party." In his criticism of the Texas lawmakers, Piker spoke about the First Amendment, claiming that those on the right are often given more freedom than those on the left. HASAN PIKER POINTS THE FINGER AT AIPAC AS DEMOCRATS SPEAK OUT AGAINST HIM "I want to talk about the hypocrisy of free speech," Piker said. "It seems to only go in one direction, right? You can't have an opinion that's outside of the permission structure, and the permission structure year over year seems to swing wide in the right direction." CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP Despite the bipartisan backlash, the event at UT Austin was relatively smooth and proceeded without any major disruptions. After his speech wrapped, Piker thanked the audience on his livestream and admitted that while he was apprehensive about being in Texas, the turnout proved the demand for progressive voices even in a red state.
