articles.title: ‘I was sure I was going to die’: Inside the Flydubai flight where passengers fought off a terrifying attack
articles.summary: A horrific mid-air catastrophe on an Emirati plane heading to Tel Aviv was averted in a stunning turn of events on Wednesday when passengers and crew bravely rushed into the cockpit and regained control of the aircraft.
articles.body: A horrific mid-air catastrophe on a plane heading to Tel Aviv was averted in a stunning turn of events on Wednesday when passengers and crew bravely rushed into the cockpit and regained control of the aircraft. Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said a pilot stabbed his colleague on a Flydubai plane and tried to “sabotage the aircraft’s system.” It plunged the aircraft thousands of feet in two minutes, causing panic and forcing the flight to make an emergency landing in Saudi Arabia. The pilot who allegedly tried to crash the plane has yet to be named. The other pilot, identified as Smit Machchhar from India, fought back and “managed to prevent a 9/11 disaster,” Netanyahu told CNN’s Jim Sciutto. “What distinguishes this incident from the other tragic attacks was at this time, the good guys won,” Netanyahu said. A spokesperson for the airline said that on-duty Flydubai crew members “successfully secured” the aircraft and landed it safely at Saudi Arabia’s Tabuk Airport, where passengers boarded onto a different flight to return to Israel. The suspected attacker has since been detained and is being questioned by Saudi authorities, Netanyahu added, but questions remain around how the incident unfolded and what motivated the pilot to instigate the bloody altercation. What happened onboard? Flydubai flight FZ1073 departed Dubai at 6:05 a.m. local time (10:05 p.m. ET) and began flying west to its destination near Tel Aviv. About two hours after taking off, the aircraft began quickly losing altitude and turned sharply to the north, flight tracking data showed. It descended 17,400 feet in just under two minutes. The flight issued a distress call at 8:31 a.m., minutes before it squawked code 7500 — the International Civil Aviation Organization code to signal an aircraft hijacking. Passengers described chaotic scenes on board the plane as the plane nosedived. “We just felt the plane drop completely and start spinning a little, and everyone was screaming, there were children crying,” passenger Mika Bauman told CNN. “I was just sure I was going to die,” she said. Other passengers took it upon themselves to charge into the cockpit and fight the attacker. Yaniv Hayoun, who recounted to Netanyahu how he put the alleged attacker in a chokehold and dragged him out of the cockpit with other passengers. Hayoun said he then grabbed the plane’s controls to help bring it back under control. Dr. Shota Musaev, a dentist on board, told CNN he tied the attacker up using headphone cords and plastic zipties. He then started tending to the wounded pilot. Even after the attacker was restrained, passengers remained terrified. “There was nothing but desert beneath us; we feared being taken to an enemy country or landing in the middle of the desert,” Assaf Rajuan told CNN. “We didn’t know who to trust.” How did the plane land? In another extraordinary turn of events, there were people on board the flight who knew how to fly a plane and were able to bring the aircraft safely down. Netanyahu and Flydubai confirmed that reserve pilots who were in the passenger area managed to regain control of the aircraft. The flight was diverted to Saudi Arabia’s Tabuk Airport, where it touched down at 9:54 a.m. David Soucie, a CNN aviation safety analyst, said it was fairly uncommon for additional on-duty pilots to be on flights “unless they are being repositioned for other flights.” What happened to the pilots? Video shared on social media and verified by CNN showed a gruesome scene onboard following the attack, where a seriously wounded pilot is seen lying on the floor of the aircraft, his pained face partially covered with a mask. The man is seen clutching his torso with his bloodied hands. He seems in pain, but conscious. Several passengers are seen helping him and monitoring his vital signs. Just next to him, guarded by several men, is another pilot — the man the flight’s passengers allege was the attacker. He too is wounded, lying on his side, his white shirt soaked with blood around his stomach. The pilot who was stabbed on the Flydubai flight suffered “massive blood loss” and was “severely wounded,” Musaev, told CNN. “He was covered in cuts — his head, his hands — they were practically sliced open, almost severed in two.” Netanyahu identified the stabbed pilot as Smit Machchhar, praising the captain as a “true hero” who demonstrated “extraordinary bravery” and saved the lives of 174 people. “Despite being stabbed and seriously injured, he fought back, resisted, opened the cockpit door, and enabled passengers and crew to overpower the attacker — preventing a catastrophic mid-air disaster,” he wrote on X. Both the captain and co-pilot of the plane were taken to the hospital, Saudi Arabia’s leading aviation operator said. Who was the attacker? What remains unclear is the identity of the pilot who allegedly attacked Machchhar. Nor do we know his motive or the weapon he used in the violent altercation. One Israeli official said that the alleged attacker was an Omani national. Oman and Israel do not have formal diplomatic relations, and it is not yet clear how the Omani pilot would have obtained clearance to fly to Israel. Where are the passengers now? The passengers, who Netanyahu said were “almost all” Israeli, have since traveled to Israel on a substitute Flydubai plane that was sent to Saudi Arabia, their family members told CNN. Prior to their arrival, at Israel’s Ben Gurion airport, the families of passengers anxiously waited for their loved ones, with some carrying balloons reading “welcome” and “it’s so good to have you back home.” After landing in Israel, Flydubai passengers were directed to a “dedicated reception area” where they met with medical teams and underwent examinations, an Israel Airports Authority spokesperson said. A 50-year-old male passenger was taken to a hospital with an upper-body injury and is in “light condition,” according to the spokesperson. Several Israeli officials commended the bravery of those on board the plane. Israeli President Isaac Herzog said the incident ended in a “great miracle,” adding that Israel and the UAE will “investigate the incident in depth together.” Four American citizens who also hold Israeli nationality were among the passengers on board, according to two US officials. What will the investigation look like? Authorities continue to unpack the details around the harrowing incident, many of which remain murky. A host of Israeli agencies, including Shin Bet, Mossad, the military and the country’s transportation ministry, are involved in investigating the Flydubai incident that took place this morning, an Israeli official told CNN. One of the main questions being looked into is why the flight crew included a pilot from a country with which Israel does not have diplomatic relations, the official said. There will also be an investigation in Saudi Arabia, who now have custody of the alleged attacker. Saudi Arabia is another Gulf nation that does not have formal diplomatic ties with Israel. Israel enforces some of the strictest aviation security protocols in the world, after facing a history of hijackings and terminal attacks. Departing passengers are required to undergo pre-screening and questioning, in addition to multiple passport checks, advanced baggage scanning, and, sometimes, full-body screening. Foreign airlines must obtain approval from Israel’s Aviation Security Operation Center before they can operate to and from the country’s airports. Investigators will likely explore the flight data recorder and cockpit voice recorder first, Marco Chan, a senior lecturer in aviation operations at London’s Kingston University, told CNN. They will also interview the crew, the off-duty pilots and passengers, and determine how the cockpit door was opened, how the weapon came to be on board, and the pilot’s medical and training history, he said. How are countries responding to the security incident? Israel’s Foreign Minister Gideon Sa’ar spoke to his UAE counterpart, Foreign Minister Abdullah bin Zayed Al Nahyan, during which they agreed to cooperate against “extremist elements” threatening security, Israel’s Foreign Ministry said. In the meantime, Flydubai temporarily suspended flights to and from Israel while an investigation continues, a spokesperson for the airline said later on Wednesday. US President Donald Trump said he spoke to Netanyahu on Wednesday, calling the passengers’ efforts to subdue the attacker “the most amazing stuff.” British Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband said he is “deeply concerned” over the events, but “very relieved that the plane landed safely thanks to the actions of those on board.” CNN’s Catherine Nichols, Ivana Kottasová, Zeena Saifi, Dana Karni, Michael Rios, Hira Humayun, Jeremy Diamond, Adam Cancryn, Eyad Kourdi, Sophie Tanno, and Billy Stockwell contributed to this report.

articles.title: SIR suspended electoral system, says ‘follow software, not law’: Bombay HC
articles.summary: PANAJI: The Bombay high court Wednesday came down heavily on the Election Commission and said it was “perturbed” by the SIR process followed by the panel.
articles.body: PANAJI: The Bombay high court Wednesday came down heavily on the Election Commission and said it was “perturbed” by the SIR process followed by the panel.Questioning EC regarding the provisions of Representation of People Act, 1950 and the Registration of Electors Rules, the division bench of Justices Valmiki Menezes and Amit Jamsandekar said: “SIR effectively by whatever instructions, has suspended the full system. It suspends Section 22, Rule 21 A and all those rules and says forget about all the laws. Now you follow the software. It cannot be like this. What is the explanation for this?”The court was hearing a case after six members of a family from Santa Cruz approached HC after their names were deleted from the rolls during the SIR.The names were deleted despite them filling Form 8 for change of address from one part of the constituency to another.“Show us from the Act where it empowers you to delete without hearing. If you are planning to remove someone’s name, you have to give the person an opportunity of hearing first,” the bench said.It also directed the electoral registration officer (ERO) concerned to be present in the court.Advocate Gaurish Agni, representing EC, told HC that the system did not permit processing of Form 8 during SIR, as a result of which their names were deleted.“At all points of time, as we understand, the law should work. The ERO must have the key to the software, call it a code, call it whatever key to software to open it or enter or delete pursuant to his order, with him. It cannot be with a third person,” the court said, pointing out that the ERO was helpless and dependent on the commands ERONET gave.The bench said the Act must be followed rather than the technology. “It has to work for the elector. Ultimately it is the role of the Election Commission to see that no voter is left out,” the bench said.Agni said during the SIR period, Form 8 could not be processed and no changes were effected.The court said this amounted to keeping the Act and the Rules in abeyance. “Then you’re suspending the Act and the Rules also by starting some completely alien procedure... the effect is you’re temporarily saying we’re giving a go by to Rules and Acts… they don’t exist. We will do our own thing. We are very perturbed by this and the effect of this. Here are six voters. We are wondering how many more there are who have not come to court,” the bench said.Agni said some voters whose names were deleted were included after they filled Form 6 and he pointed out that the family hadn’t submitted enumeration forms and refused to fill Form 6.“You have no business asking them to fill Form 6 because the system didn’t allow you to do it on Form 8. That was the problem,” the bench said.“SIR, first of all, doesn’t fit as a standalone proceeding. SIR has to fit basically under Rule 13 read with Section 22. You can conduct as many revisions as you want but even if there’s no revision being conducted, any elector new or who is moving from one ward or part to another can under Form 6, 7, 8 present it at any time. There are no fetters under the Act. All we are saying is when revision comes, it cannot override these provisions,” the bench said. Agni said EC had no intention to delete anybody on purpose.“You cannot delete anybody without hearing that person. articles.title: Netanyahu praises heroic bystander in bloody cockpit attack for preventing ‘another 9/11’
articles.summary: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu praised the heroic passenger who stormed the cockpit as the FlyDubai plane plunged 13,000 feet in one minute.
articles.body: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu addressed the bloody cockpit attack that occurred on a flight headed from Dubai to Tel Aviv during an exclusive interview with Fox News on Wednesday. Netanyahu recounted how the event unfolded and praised the "unbelievable courage" of passengers who quickly corralled the alleged attacker and stabilized the plane, specially crediting Yaniv Chayon, the man who broke into the cockpit and tamed the attacker. The prime minister said he prevented the world from a disaster of "unbelievable proportions." "The passengers, including 30 children, are already saying their prayers. They know they're gone from this world," he told "Hannity." "And this young man just acts with incredible, incredible heroism and saves the day." FLYDUBAI PILOT STABS FELLOW PILOT, ATTEMPTS TO CRASH PLANE, NETANYAHU SAYS "He acted with coolness of judgment and heroism… just tremendous courage that prevented another 9/11." The 9/11 terrorist attacks killed nearly 3,000 people. MIKE PENCE: REMEMBER THE FALLEN — AND THE GENERATION THAT DEFENDED AMERICA SINCE 9/11 A pilot aboard the Israel-bound FlyDubai flight allegedly stabbed another pilot and apparently attempted to "crash the plane" with more than 100 people onboard — an incident authorities describe as a suspected hijacking. The wounded captain unlocked the cockpit door, letting in passengers who worked together to subdue the attacker and stabilize the nosediving aircraft. UNITED FLIGHT FROM CHICAGO MAKES EMERGENCY LANDING AFTER PASSENGER'S 'MULTIPLE ATTEMPTS' TO BREACH COCKPIT Netanyahu met with Chayon earlier on Wednesday, lauding his act of courage and praising him for taking control of the plane under "impossible" circumstances. "I met with this Israeli, this unbelievable Israeli. His name is Yaniv, who did this thing," he explained. "And I asked him, ‘How did you do it?’ And he said, ‘Well, I just had to do it.’" MIDAIR BRAWL ERUPTS ON PACKED FLIGHT AS SCREAMING PASSENGERS JUMP FROM SEATS "His family was there, 174 passengers, most of whom were Israelis, were there. He had to save them." Netanyahu blamed "hatred" for the attack and said it was rooted in antisemitism and that many have "fallen prey" to what he described as "propaganda" that vilifies Israel. ANTISEMITIC VIOLENCE REACHES DEADLIEST LEVEL SINCE 1994, NEW GLOBAL REPORT FINDS "I don't know the exact background of this person, the attacker, but he obviously hated Israelis because he was going to kill about 170 of them on this plane, killing himself, too," the prime minister said. "That's fanaticism and hatred of an incalculable level." While the captain was incapacitated, the aircraft dropped from 30,000 feet to 17,000 in roughly one minute before it diverted to Saudi Arabia, according to flight radar. Other pilots aboard the aircraft took control and landed it safely. The pilot of Flight 1073 has been identified as Capt. Smit Machchhar. Netanyahu says he is "fighting for his life" after sustaining severe injuries. PLANE PASSENGERS SCREAM IN HARROWING MID-FLIGHT VIDEO AS VIOLENT SHAKING SENDS CABIN CEILING PANELS FLYING "Apparently, he stabbed him, or he hit him with an ax. He was bleeding profusely. The plane began to go out of control and began a nosedive," Netanyahu said. "The pilot who was there was an Indian pilot with sort of a very badly wounded. He's fighting, I think, for his life right now, but in an act of unbelievable courage, he managed to unlock the door to the cockpit." AMERICANS WARNED AGAIN TO RETHINK TRAVEL AS MISSILE ATTACK RATTLES HISTORIC REGION CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP Netanyahu told Reuters that the alleged cockpit attacker was arrested after the plane made an emergency landing in Tabuk, Saudi Arabia. An Israeli official identified the co-pilot as an Omani national. FlyDubai cautioned that the suspect’s motive remains unknown and declared that all flights in and out of Israel will be suspended while the investigation is carried out. Israeli officials say investigators are working to examine the co-pilot’s motive and whether he acted alone. "Just think about it... If you're next hijacked, make sure an Israeli is sitting next to you," Netanyahu said.

articles.title: UK says Iran may be linked to alleged airbase plot, drawing angry denial
articles.summary: Andy Burnham says UK has ‘strong indications’ Iran involved in alleged security incident at RAF base used by US.
articles.body:
The United Kingdom’s Prime Minister Andy Burnham has said there are “strong indications” that Iran played a role in an alleged security incident at an airbase used by the United States, prompting a forceful denial by Tehran.

Burnham told the BBC broadcaster on Wednesday that investigations into the suspected plot at the Royal Air Force base in Fairford were ongoing. Five British men in their 20s were arrested near the base on Sunday, on suspicion of “terrorism” and explosives offences. They were all released on bail a day later.

“There are strong indications that Iran played a part in what happened over the weekend at RAF Fairford, but of course it remains an ongoing, complex and serious police investigation,” Burnham said. “We are working closely with our colleagues in the United States of America.”

He did not provide details about what the suspects were planning or why the UK thinks Iran was involved.

But the prime minister said he would “update people more in due course”.

Burnham’s comments marked the first time a British official had publicly linked Iran to the events at the base.

Iran, however, has strongly denied any involvement in the incident and the country’s foreign minister, Abbas Araghchi, hit back at Burnham’s allegations.

“PM Burnham says the UK Government ‘can confirm our belief that we believe Iran to have played a part’ in the RAF Fairford incident,” he wrote on X. “I can confirm Iran’s belief that releasing supposed terrorists working for foreign states really says it all. You’re barking up the wrong tree.”

The RAF base 160km west of London has been used by US bombers during decades of conflicts in the Middle East, including the US and Israel’s war on Iran, which began in February. Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) has previously said that it considers any base used to attack its territory a legitimate target.

After three days of investigations, including using a bomb disposal team, police said Tuesday they had found no explosives in the vehicles, but they had retrieved a “quantity of petrol”.

Top US officials have meanwhile criticised the decision to grant the suspects bail, with President Donald Trump saying “I wouldn’t have done that” and Secretary of State Marco Rubio saying a lot of people were “disturbed” by the move.

Laurence Taylor, the head of British counterterror policing, said on Tuesday that the suspects remain under investigation and the decision to grant bail was grounded in “experience and strategy”.

He said a line of inquiry is whether the suspected offences were committed by “proxies or individuals, either knowingly or unknowingly, working on behalf of a foreign state”.

Adding ⁠to the intrigue around Sunday’s events, The Times reported that one of the men called emergency services shortly before being arrested in the early hours.

“Whether it was surveillance, a ‘dry run’ to test security or a stunt to ‌send a message to the British government are all under consideration,” The Times said, adding that investigators were unsure whether he got cold feet or it was part ‌of ‌a plan.

Police declined to comment on whether one of the suspects had made the call.

articles.title: AFCON 2027: East Africa races to get tournament-ready
articles.summary: Kenya, Uganda and Tanzania have less than nine months to prepare for AFCON 2027.
articles.body:
Nairobi, Kenya – With less than nine months until the 2027 Africa Cup of Nations kicks off, Kenya, Uganda and Tanzania are entering the most demanding phase of preparations: completing and testing the stadiums, training grounds and supporting infrastructure needed to host the tournament.

The tournament, scheduled for June 19 to July 17, 2027, will be the first Africa Cup of Nations jointly hosted by three countries and the competition’s return to East Africa since Ethiopia staged the finals in 1976.

A Confederation of African Football (CAF) delegation spent eight days inspecting facilities across the three host countries earlier this month, assessing stadiums, training grounds, hotels, airports and other infrastructure. The delegation included officials responsible for competitions, safety and security, transport, media, television and logistics.

In Kenya, the biggest project is the newly built Talanta Sports International Stadium in Nairobi.

The 60,000-capacity stadium is intended to be the country’s flagship AFCON venue and was inspected by CAF earlier this month. During a subsequent visit, CAF President Patrice Motsepe said he was impressed by the progress at Talanta. He also visited Kasarani Stadium, where work remains to be completed.

But Kenya’s preparations extend well beyond its new flagship stadium.

CAF’s inspection also covered training venues, hotels, airport infrastructure and other sites supporting the Nairobi tournament operation.

Nicholus Musonye, chairman of Kenya’s AFCON 2027 Local Organising Committee, told Al Jazeera that the country was addressing the outstanding requirements.

“I want to assure Africa, and I want to assure the world, that Kenya, Uganda, Tanzania, we are ready to host AFCON,” Musonye said.

He said work on Kasarani’s pitch should be completed by the end of October, with the venue planned to be ready for handover in December.

But concerns remain about some of the facilities that will support the tournament.

Kelvin Kimaru, a Kenyan football fan, told Al Jazeera that training grounds remained a concern.

“We are not yet ready because the training grounds for the coming teams are not yet ready,” Kimaru said.

Moses Kamalik, an executive member of the Boxing Federation of Kenya, said other venues also needed work, including Nyayo Stadium and Kipchoge Keino Stadium in Eldoret.

The challenge for Kenya is broader than completing Talanta; it needs a network of match venues, training grounds and supporting facilities capable of operating together when teams and supporters arrive.

Tanzania: the race extends beyond stadiums

Tanzania is also entering the final stretch, with preparations covering stadiums, training grounds and the infrastructure connecting them.

Neema Msitha, chief executive of the country’s AFCON 2027 Local Organising Committee, told Al Jazeera that the country’s stadiums were more than 80 percent complete on average and expected to be ready for handover to CAF in January.

“All these stadiums are almost ready. If you grade them on average, all of them are almost above 80 percent,” Msitha said.

Training facilities are being developed alongside the main venues, with five facilities being prepared in each host location. Msitha said they were about 75 percent complete.

The Tanzanian government has also applied pressure to accelerate the work.

In August, Prime Minister Mwigulu Nchemba ordered work on AFCON training grounds to speed up, saying the facilities needed to be completed on time and meet CAF standards. He issued the directive after inspecting the Farasi and Leaders Club training grounds in Dar-es-Salaam.

Road infrastructure is also part of the preparations. In June, Works Minister Abdallah Ulega ordered contractors working on roads linked to the tournament in Arusha to operate around the clock to meet deadlines and international standards.

Msitha pointed to regional airlines, Air Tanzania and ferry services between Dar-es-Salaam and Zanzibar as part of the transport arrangements being developed for teams, officials and supporters.

CAF’s September inspection included Benjamin Mkapa Stadium in Dar-es-Salaam and other key facilities in Tanzania as the governing body continued to assess preparations across the three hosts.

Uganda is working towards the same year-end push.

Patrick Ogwel, a CAF infrastructure monitoring officer, told Al Jazeera that infrastructure development was expected to be ready by December 31.

Hoima City Stadium has been completed and commissioned, he said, while Akii-Bua Olympic Stadium in Lira is due to be completed and commissioned by December.

Uganda’s Local Organising Committee has identified Akii-Bua, Hoima City Stadium and Mandela National Stadium as its three main stadiums. It expects 10 of the country’s 12 training facilities to be ready by the end of the year.

The organising committee said after CAF’s latest inspection that all three stadiums remained on course for completion by the end of December, while some training facilities were planned to be completed in January 2027.

But the deadlines are not without pressure.

On September 24, Uganda’s State Minister for Sports Peter Ogwang directed the Uganda People’s Defence Forces to accelerate work on several AFCON training facilities, citing concerns about the pace of construction at sites including Pece Stadium in Gulu, Lira and Gulu University.

After its September inspection, the CAF delegation also briefed President Yoweri Museveni, with challenges outside Kampala among the issues raised during the assessment.

From construction to tournament readiness

The coming months will test whether the three hosts can turn construction progress into a functioning tournament operation.

AFCON requires stadiums and training grounds that can handle teams and spectators while meeting requirements for broadcasting, media, security, transport, hospitality and match operations.

A completed stadium is only one part of the equation.

Kenya, Tanzania and Uganda have already gained experience from jointly hosting the 2024 African Nations Championship, which allowed the three countries to work together on a major continental tournament. CAF has also involved representatives from the three local organising committees in an observer mission at the recent AFCON in Morocco.

But AFCON will be a larger undertaking, with 24 national teams competing across the three countries for almost a month.

The coming months will determine whether the work under way across the three countries can be completed, verified and brought into operation before teams and supporters begin arriving.

For supporters in East Africa, the tournament represents more than a test of stadiums and infrastructure. It is also a chance to experience Africa’s biggest national-team competition on home soil.

Gilbert Okeya, a Kenyan football fan and Football Kenya Federation referee, told Al Jazeera:

“We are happy because we are going to host, and we are going to have an opportunity to have live matches for AFCON in our country.”

articles.title: Pakistan says 22 fighters killed in air attacks on Afghanistan
articles.summary: Kabul says the strikes on Kunar and Helmand provinces killed nine women and children.
articles.body:
Pakistan has launched air attacks on Afghanistan, saying it targeted “camps and hideouts” used by armed groups in two locations and killed an estimated 22 fighters.

The announcement by Pakistan’s Ministry of Information on Thursday came as Kabul accused Islamabad of killing at least nine women and children in attacks on its Kunar and Helmand provinces.

Al Jazeera could not independently verify the casualty claims.

Zabihullah Mujahid, the spokesman for Afghanistan’s government, said the strikes took place late on Wednesday and that at least nine people were killed and 11 others wounded.

In a post on X, he said the attacks on northeastern Kunar and southern Helmand destroyed three houses.

“We condemn this act and consider it an aggression and crime against all accepted principles,” he wrote.

The alleged attacks come amid an escalation in fighting between the neighbouring countries after three months of relative calm. Islamabad accuses Kabul of harbouring armed groups, including the Tehrik-i-Taliban Pakistan, who stage cross-border attacks on its territory.

The Afghan government ‌denies the charge and says the Pakistani attacks have targeted civilian homes, killing and wounding women and children.

articles.title: Indian pilot who fought off apparent hijack attempt hailed as hero as Flydubai passengers describe terror onboard
articles.summary: Authorities are investigating how and why a pilot allegedly stabbed his colleague on a Flydubai flight to Tel Aviv on Wednesday, sending the plane into a terrifying nosedive and forcing the flight to make an emergency landing in Saudi Arabia. Follow for live updates.
articles.body:
• Disaster averted: An Indian pilot and passengers who thwarted an apparent attempted hijacking of a Dubai-to-Tel Aviv flight have been hailed as heroes. The pilot — identified as Captain Smit Machchhar — “managed to prevent a 9/11 disaster,” Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu told CNN .

• Terrifying moments: Passengers rushed the cockpit as Machchhar’s colleague attacked him and the plane plummeted 17,400 feet in less than two minutes. The plane was later diverted to Saudi Arabia and passengers have since returned safely to Israel. Flydubai has launched an investigation, an airline spokesperson said.

• Questions remain: Israel has called the incident an “attempted terrorist attack,” but no motive has been confirmed. The attacker has not been identified , but one Israeli official said he is an Omani national.

Israel’s national airline El Al said it is working on evacuating Israelis stranded in Dubai after Flydubai suspended flights to Tel Aviv following Wednesday’s stabbing and attempted hijacking.

There is no date set yet for the evacuation flights, an El Al spokesperson told CNN.

Flights between Dubai International Airport (DXB) and Ben Gurion Airport (TLV) have increased in recent years. The signing of the Abraham Accords in 2020 normalized relations between Israel and the United Arab Emirates (UAE) and allowed commercial aviation services between the two countries to resume.

Flydubai typically operates 70 flights from Dubai to Tel Aviv weekly. It has been the sole carrier on the route in recent months after Israeli carriers suspended flights to Dubai due to the Iran war.

More than 1 million Israeli passengers traveled to Dubai in 2025, according to data from TLV airport.

Eighteen years before Captain Smit Machchhar was hailed for helping save a Flydubai flight from Dubai to Tel Aviv, he was a teenager learning to fly at the bottom of New Zealand’s South Island.

Philip Kean, CEO of Mainland Air in Dunedin, remembers him from that first spell away from home in 2008.

Aged around 20 at the time, Machchhar was one of a group of young Indian flying students training in near Dunedin Airport and living at an old priests seminary in nearby Mosgiel.

“He got through in the required time, and obviously the rest of the story is history,” Kean said.

Machchhar later returned to India, joined an airline and, in time, became a captain.

The school’s care of the students, often abroad for the first time, went beyond the cockpit. “We take them into our custody and look after them in their accommodation,” Kean said. “Sort of part of the big family, extended family.”

Watching the news of Machchhar’s heroic actions from Dunedin, Kean said “It was an amazing feat,” and that he was “very proud” of his former student handled the situation.

Kean still has a group photograph from those days long before the world knew Machchhar’s name. “He definitely got a smile of his own… he’s sort of a happy, happy chap.”

The Flydubai attempted hijacking adds to a year of crisis for Middle East airlines, which are already suffering from slowing ticket sales and rising fuel prices caused by war in the region.

The Gulf kingdoms have invested billions to build themselves into world class travel and transit hubs.

But travelers have become increasingly reluctant to transit through international hubs like Dubai, after the US-led war in Iran stranded thousands of passengers earlier this year. In August, air travel demand for Middle East carriers fell 14.6% year-over-year, compared to a 0.6% increase outside the region, the International Air Transport Association said .

The recent incident could further discourage regional travel and increase pressure to improve security measures among Middle Eastern airlines. Israel said it would ramp up security checks after one of the pilots appeared to attempt to crash the flight from Dubai to Tel Aviv.

According to the IATA, the conflict in the Middle East is expected to halve profitability for airlines this year compared to 2025.

The industry is already grappling with rising operational expenses, higher fuel costs and a growing global shortage of aircraft personnel. Consulting firm Oliver Wyman estimated the shortfall of pilots would peak this year at about 24,000.

The World Economic Forum also warned that falling tourism in the Middle East would have broader economic implications, as an industry that accounted for about $11.6 trillion in global GDP last year and supported 357 million jobs.

As investigators probe the apparent attempted hijacking of a Flydubai plane, they will be looking to answer a number of key questions, said CNN’s senior national security analyst, Juliette Kayyem.

The alleged assailant’s motives are not yet clear, and authorities have not yet released his identity. But “any investigator would begin with the idea that this was a terrorist attack,” since it was a flight headed for Israel with many Israelis on board, she said.

There are other possible theories, too – and authorities will be investigating whether there were any mental health factors, potential radicalization, and whether he had any co-conspirators or was enabled by any particular country.

The incident also raised serious security questions, Kayyem said, such as how the assailant, a pilot, managed to get to this position without having been caught or detected before – since all pilots are continuously assessed, including their politics or risk of radicalization.

It was thanks to the quick thinking of the assailant’s colleague, who was attacked in the cockpit and is now being treated in hospital, that likely disaster was averted, Kayyem said. “I will say the pilot who was stabbed, his ability to think that he needed to open that (cockpit) door saved over 100 people’s lives today.”

Authorities are investigating how and why a pilot allegedly stabbed his colleague on a Flydubai flight to Tel Aviv on Wednesday, sending the plane into a terrifying nosedive, causing panic onboard and forcing the flight to make an emergency landing in Saudi Arabia.

We’re learning more details about the horrifying and heroic scenes onboard after passengers and crew bravely rushed into the cockpit, thwarting the apparent hijack attempt, and landed the plane safely.

Pilot hailed a hero: Captain Smit Machchhar, the Indian pilot who was stabbed mid-air, has been hailed as a hero by Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Israeli Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, who told CNN Machchhar “managed to prevent a 9/11 disaster.” Machchhar is in stable condition and being treated at a hospital in Saudi Arabia, according to the Indian Embassy in Riyadh.

Questions remain about attacker: The pilot who allegedly attacked Machchhar has not been identified, but one Israeli official said he is an Omani national. The suspect has since been detained and is being questioned by Saudi authorities, Netanyahu said Wednesday.

The investigation: Israeli officials have called the incident an “attempted terrorist attack,” but no motive has been confirmed. Netanyahu said Israel did not have any warning or intelligence about the incident. Flydubai flights to and from Israel are temporarily suspended. Meanwhile, Foreign Minister Gideon Sa’ar discussed the incident with his UAE counterpart and they agreed to cooperate against “extremist elements” threatening security.

Distress call: Flydubai flight FZ1074 left Dubai at 6:05 a.m. local time Wednesday. About two hours later, the aircraft began quickly losing altitude and turned sharply to the north. The flight issued a distress call at 8:31 a.m., minutes before it squawked code 7500 — the International Civil Aviation Organization code to signal an aircraft hijacking.

Passengers scramble: After the cockpit door was thrust open, passengers raced to restrain the alleged attacker while others tended to a seriously wounded Machchhar. Passenger Adam Polo said it felt like he was riding “the craziest roller coaster” as the plane plunged 17,400 feet, while others on board said they thought they were going to die.

Safely diverted: Netanyahu and Flydubai said reserve pilots in the passenger area managed to regain control of the aircraft and land it safely at Saudi Arabia’s Tabuk Airport, where it touched down at 9:54 a.m.

Passengers reach Israel: The passengers then traveled on a substitute Flydubai plane to their final destination Tel Aviv, where they reunited with loved ones and received medical care.

Passengers on board the Flydubai flight have described scenes of “complete chaos” and a “nightmare” as the plane plunged repeatedly, prompting some to say goodbye to their families.

Passenger Adam Polo, who was on the plane with his wife and two young children, recalled the terror of its sudden descent during the attack in the cockpit.

Polo described the descent as “the craziest roller coaster that you ever did, but multiplied by a thousand.” He recalled how people near the cockpit started shouting, “there is stabbing,” and that “everything was full of blood.”

Passenger Assaf Rajuan said that even after the attacker on the Flydubai flight to Israel was restrained, passengers remained terrified , not knowing who to trust and fearing a hostage situation.

Passengers didn’t even know if the person in control of the plane “was on our side, or who was on which side,” he added.

Flydubai passenger Mika Bauman described chaos aboard the flight that was diverted to Saudi Arabia, as children cried and passengers screamed.

“I was just sure I was going to die,” she said. “You’re just sitting there and accepting your fate.”

CNN’s Erin Burnett, Dana Karni, Hira Humayun, Jeremy Diamond, and Zeena Saifi contributed reporting.

Captain Smit Machchhar has been identified as the Indian pilot who was stabbed while helping thwart the apparent attempt to hijack the Flydubai plane en route to Israel on Wednesday.

Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu praised Machchhar as a “true hero, ” saying he prevented “disaster for Israel” and saved the lives of the 174 people on the plane.

Netanyahu concluded by saying he wished “Captain Machchhar a speedy and full recovery.”

His condition: Machchhar suffered “massive blood loss” and was “severely wounded,” Dr. Shota Musaev, a dentist on board, told CNN. Video shared on social media and verified by CNN showed the pilot seriously wounded on the floor of the aircraft. Several passengers can be seen helping him and monitoring his vital signs.

Once the plane landed, Machchhar was taken to hospital in Tabuk, Saudi Arabia. The Indian Embassy in Riyadh earlier said he was in “stable condition” but was awaiting a full update on his health.

A hero: Machchhar has also been hailed as a hero in his home country, with leading news outlets praising his bravery. Many Indians have also taken to social media to express their pride.

The identity of the pilot who allegedly attacked Captain Smit Machchhar — the pilot who fought back in the attempted hijacking of the Israel-bound Flydubai flight FZ107 — remains unclear.

Nor do we know the other pilot’s motive or the weapon he used in the violent altercation.

One Israeli official said the alleged attacker was an Omani national.

Oman and Israel do not have formal diplomatic relations, and it is not yet clear how the Omani pilot would have obtained clearance to fly to Israel. The suspected attacker has since been detained and is being questioned by Saudi authorities, Netanyahu said Wednesday.

But questions remain around how the incident unfolded and what motivated the pilot to instigate the bloody interaction.

Passengers arrived safely in Israel on a replacement Flydubai flight after Saudi Arabia rejected an Israeli request to send a military or civilian plane to bring passengers home. One passenger, Assaf Rajuan, said the person who attacked Machchhar was “neutralized” very quickly by a group of passengers and flight crew.

Rajuan said he and about five others helped subdue the attacker.

Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said the pilot on board the diverted Flydubai flight who fought back after another pilot in the cockpit appears to have tried to crash the plane “managed to prevent a 9/11 disaster.”

“That’s what it looks like was happening as far as the specific motivations of this,” he told CNN’s Jim Sciutto.

He said that he spoke with US President Donald Trump “about this amazing, amazing act of heroism that saved a disaster that would have been not only a disaster for Israel, but you can imagine how it could affect the global aviation.”

He went on to say that Israel did not have any warning or intelligence about the incident and that an investigation into it is underway.

“I spoke again to President (Sheikh Mohammed) bin Zahed of the United Arab Emirates, and he agreed immediately that we should join the investigation. And we’ll find out.”

Israel has called the incident an attempted terrorist attack, but has not made public the details behind the attacker’s motive.

articles.title: The world’s busiest island holds some of the planet’s greatest ancient treasures
articles.summary: The island of Java is home to 150 million people but also incredible cultural treasures including the grand Buddhist temple of Borobudur and the ancient cultural kingdom of Yogyakarta.
articles.body: In the frenetic, action-packed metropolis of Jakarta, a democratically elected president oversees Indonesia’s government. But just a few hours east, a sultan still holds court. Yogyakarta is a rare thing, a sultan’s kingdom inside of a country that is otherwise a republic. In the local Javanese language, the letter Y is pronounced like a hard J, with the city’s name shortened to “Jogja.” Here in Jogja, a city whose backbone was built along an ancient cosmological axis, the present always exists door-to-door with the past. The modern city is full of noise and color. Red coolers proffer bottles of Indonesia’s ubiquitous Bintang beer. Striped curtains shade roadside cafes. Street art pulls inspiration from ancient batik prints. Local-language pop ballads and American rap music blast from speakers. While Jogja’s car traffic can rival Jakarta’s at peak times, the city’s heart has a different feel. The narrow streets around the sultan’s palace are filled with backpackers, street vendors, tour guides hawking their services, and office workers popping out for a coffee amid the madness. More than 150 million people live on Java, Indonesia’s economic and political core and the world’s most populous island. It’s crammed with treasures too. Within a 25-mile radius, there are three UNESCO World Heritage sites. The first of these is Yogyakarta itself. Its ancient center was built in the mid-1700s in an auspicious location chosen for its proximity to points on land and in the heavens. Its most important building, the Kraton or Sultan’s Palace, was placed equidistant between the Indian Ocean to the south and the still-active volcano Mount Merapi to the north. The country that became modern Indonesia once had multiple sultans, but Yogyakarta’s stood up to support the republican opposition to Dutch colonial rule after World War II, and was allowed to keep his domain when an independent federal government took power. Kraton is the ideal place to begin a trip to central Java, and it’s also a starting point for understanding Yogyakarta. Though it’s still the home of the sultan, Hamengkubuwono X, and his family, much of the space is open to the public. The entry fee includes a guide, and it’s worth it — every structure, from the glass pavilion decorated with images of musical instruments to the sculptures of mythological animals flanking entryways — has deep symbolic meaning that many visitors would likely miss. Also nearby is Tamansari. Sometimes written as two words, Taman Sari, the name means “perfumed garden” or “beautiful garden,” it’s usually called the water castle. It’s easy to see why — the striking water feature in the center of the palace complex is greenish or blue depending on the sun. It was designed in a mix of Dutch and Indonesian heritage styles, perfectly encapsulating the contradictions that make Jogja so irresistibly compelling. By following the walkway past the exit, you can explore the area now known as the Tamansari Tourist Village. Here, more modern Indonesian artists paint murals, sell traditional crafts like batik cloth and finely wrought silver jewelry, and make lattes from Java’s world-famous civet coffee. A millennium in a day It’s possible to travel back hundreds of years in a short time by visiting two world heritage-listed temples just outside of Yogyakarta. The most famous of Java’s historic places is Borobudur, one of the grandest Buddhist temples in the world. These days, the most-practiced religion in Indonesia is Islam, but both Hindu and Buddhist dynasties thrived here in the 8th and 9th centuries. Borobudur, a massive, lotus-shaped temple complex with a dramatic stone front, stands majestically on a sun-soaked plain. Borobudur’s sense of spirituality still imbues the air around it. Although much of the population in Java converted to Islam and Borobudur was abandoned, it was not destroyed. According to Panggah Ardiyansyah, a Jogja native and lecturer at SOAS University in London, Borobudur is “sacred” even to this day. Locals revered the place enough to leave it alone — and believed that interfering with the site would bring bad luck. Ardiyansyah advises that people visiting Borobudur study the reliefs along the temple walls, which show scenes from the life of the Buddha. “People in the ancient times tried to tell stories using reliefs, using drawing on a wall or on statues. It’s so fascinating. You can try to understand it yourself, try to reference the manuscripts, and try to ‘read’ it.” It’s tempting to immediately climb to the top of Borobudur and take photos of the impressive surrounding landscape. A more spiritual approach is to perform pradakshina — a traditional act of circling a holy site several times in a clockwise direction. Guides recommend doing it three or more times to settle into a more meditative state of mind. The truly devout will make 108 loops, as the number is spiritually important in Buddhism. Ardiyansyah notes that many of Borobudur’s treasures have in the past been removed and taken overseas. In recent decades, the government of the Netherlands — which colonized Indonesia from the 1600s-1900s — has been in the process of repatriating sculptures, reliefs, and other items to the arts and culture administration in Java. However, many of Borobudur’s other artifacts — including Buddha heads removed from their bodies — remain in museums in the US and Europe, as well as likely in private collections. Visitors hoping to climb Borobudur must book a timed slot online ahead of arrival, as numbers are limited to 1,200 a day. On-site, they must swap their shoes for a pair of traditional, woven sandals called upanat — eco-friendly footwear, designed to protect the ancient volcanic stones, which can be kept as a souvenir. Grouped with a mandatory guide, visitors board a shuttle vehicle to the temple base. The earliest available time slot for foreign tourists is at 8:30 am, but some hotels, like the nearby ultra-luxe Amanjiwo, can arrange sunrise tours for an additional fee. The gasp-inducing scale and intricate stonework of Borobudur have attracted numerous global figures over the years. Prince Charles, former Indian Prime Minister Indira Gandhi, and Barack Obama are among the dignitaries who have walked its stone galleries and tried kunto bimo — a popular ritual where visitors reach inside a lattice-work stupa to touch a stone Buddha, with the promise that it will grant a wish. Because the practice has no roots in traditional Buddhist belief, historians and locals suspect it was cooked up as a tourist gimmick long ago, though it has since become a tradition in its own way. The Hindu temple complex of Prambanan is not as busy as its nearby Buddhist cousin, which is a bonus for travelers with limited time. No advanced bookings are required, and both temples can be visited in the same day relatively easily. Tour companies like Jogja Driver Team recommend visiting Borobudur in the morning to avoid the worst of the heat, then Prambanan after lunch. The entrance and exits of Prambanan are also cluttered with vendors selling souvenirs and cold drinks — offering a good opportunity to pick up a bottle of water. The site is large and totally open to Java’s scorching sun, so it’s important to stay hydrated. Hats, comfortable walking shoes and sunscreen are also advised. Asia travelers might get a sense of déjà vu upon first glimpsing Prambanan, Indonesia’s largest Hindu temple site. That’s because it resembles one of the region’s most famous tourist attractions — Cambodia’s Angkor Wat. The tall temples feature square bases and conical towers adorned with intricate stone carvings of gods and mythical animals, with the three largest structures dedicated to Shiva, Brahma, and Vishnu. In all, more than 200 shrines and temples are scattered across 40 hectares of land. Although Borobudur and Prambanan look and feel entirely distinct, it is almost impossible not to compare them. Many visitors are surprised that such massive monuments representing two entirely different world religions were built just a short distance apart. “A lot of people want to see it as rival cultures or rival religions, but at the time it wasn’t seen that way,” says William Chapman, who spent many years in Indonesia working on restoration projects. “Borobudur started getting attention early on, from the early 19th century. There’s a lot more sculpture, a lot of reliefs, and it was more accessible and had a good view.” Prambanan, meanwhile, was abandoned and largely neglected until the start of the 20th century, with the first restoration in the 1930s, Chapman added. While Prambanan currently sees fewer crowds than its Buddhist neighbor, Chapman believes that balance is shifting. India’s rapidly growing middle class is increasingly eager for international travel, and Chapman says there is a strong draw toward destinations with deep Hindu heritage. With Indonesia offering Indian passport holders a visa on arrival, visiting is relatively easy. Even amid crowds of tourists, blistering midday sunlight, and feet worn out from miles of walking, the sense of spirituality in Yogyakarta and its surrounding historic treasures is undeniable, It’s hard to visit these sites and not awed at the splendor of it all, and to think of the many craftspeople and builders who constructed such impressive sites without the help of technology. Even Ardiyansyah, a Jogja native, says he still feels wonder when he visits Borobudur after a long time away. Climbing to the top and looking out over the countryside is just as powerful as studying the intricate stone carvings. “You are rewarded with a view of the world.”

articles.title: The Divine Magic of True Love: Moving Beyond the Skin to the Soul
articles.summary: Why does the world suffer from so many heartaches today? We see relationships crumbling and marriages ending in separation every day.
articles.body: Why does the world suffer from so many heartaches today? We see relationships crumbling and marriages ending in separation every day. We celebrate breakups with parties, yet deep down, we remain empty and miserable. Why? Because we have misunderstood the essence of Love. We have confused the divine emotion of Love with lust, and the eternal longing of the Soul with the transient attraction of the skin. If we want to experience Everlasting Bliss and Eternal Happpiness, we must activate the Divine Magic of True Love within us.This transformation begins when we understand the four pillars of Love, learn how to make our relationships work, and move from ordinary love to True Love.The Four Pillars of LoveHave you ever stopped to contemplate what makes a relationship strong? Just as a table needs four legs to stand upright without wobbling, a lasting relationship stands on the four essential pillars of bonding.The four pillars that hold up a relationship are emotional, physical, intellectual and spiritual. Love must flow not only from the body and the heart, but from the head and the Soul too. The body expresses physical Love, the heart expresses emotional Love, the head allows intellectual Love to blossom, but it is the Soul that creates Eternal Love between two people.Most relationships rest on only the emotional and physical pillars, and couples wonder why, in time, they grow bored of each other. Without an intellectual bond, a stimulating conversation, there is nothing to sustain the connection once the initial spark settles. And even a relationship strong in all three of body, heart and head is still incomplete without the fourth and most important pillar: the Spiritual. It is only when Love flows through all four levels — body, heart, head and Soul — that a relationship becomes truly unbreakable.Many couples mistake this physical pillar for the whole of Love. But physical Love without the Love of head and heart behind it is closer to lust than Love. True Love that flows from the head and heart naturally expresses itself through the body, making that bond beautiful rather than empty. If we want our Love to be True Love, we must let it flow through all four: Body, Head, Heart and Soul.How to Make a Relationship WorkWhy are so many relationships breaking apart today? It is because Love has become transactional, full of conditions and expectations. To experience True Love, we must learn to give more than we take. Love is not a well from which we keep drawing water — pull from it endlessly, and it runs dry. Love is a fountain. The more it flows outward, the more it circulates and returns. If we try only to extract Love from a relationship instead of pouring it in, it will inevitably wither.Just as in our garden, we never forget to water our plants, yet we routinely forget to shower Love to the ones we love, taking relationships for granted until the Love has withered past return. Often, when we finally try to make up for that neglect, the effort only ends in a breakup, because True Love, when genuinely present, never reaches a point where two people consider leaving each other at all.Many couples also make the mistake of assuming that Love, once felt, does not need to be spoken. But a simple, sincerely meant expression of Love makes a tremendous difference. Partners who take the trouble to surprise each other with small, unexpected acts of Love keep that Love standing strong, rather than letting it be eroded quietly by silence.The other great destroyer of relationships is possessiveness for possessiveness is insecurity wearing the mask of Love, and it suffocates the bond it claims to protect. True Love and trust go together — where there is genuine Love, there is no room for suspicion, and where trust is missing, no relationship survives for long. If we want relationships to truly work, we must turn our Love into True Love which is transcendental and unconditional. Such a Love can never break.Moving From Love to True LoveHow do we transition from ordinary worldly love to the sublime state of True Love? We must move from the "Love of the Skin" to the "Love of the Soul." Worldly love is skin-deep, based on physical beauty, wealth, or status. Because the skin must eventually age and wither, skin-deep love is destined to fade, leaving us in agony.True Love, on the other hand, is a longing of the Soul, that Spark Of Unique Life (SOUL) within us, for the Soul in the beloved. It is the realization that the same Divine Life Energy that throbs in my heart gives life to yours. It is seeing the Divine in the beloved and in one and all.This is also the distinction older spiritual traditions have pointed toward. The Sufis called this Divine Love Ishq-e-Haqiqi, distinct from the worldly Ishq-e-Majazi, and the Greeks separated Agape from Eros similarly. Love flows from SIP, the Supreme Immortal Power, that we call, God, to our individual Spark Of Unique Life. True Love is this Divine current flowing between two Souls, asking for nothing in return.In True Love, we do not fall — we rise. The world's ordinary language treats Love as something we stumble into and eventually fall out of, but True Love lifts us, because it flows from the Divine within one Soul to the Divine within another, not merely from skin to skin. When we see God in the one we love, and love God in all, there is no longer an "I" and a "you" — there is only Oneness. This is the ultimate secret: build your Love on all four pillars and let it rise until it becomes True Love — Divine, unconditional and eternal.Authored by AiR - Atman in Ravi

articles.title: TOI Healing India Forum 2026: Celebrating the people shaping India’s wellness journey; Nominate now
articles.summary: The wellness journey has never been a one-size-fits-all experience.
articles.body: The wellness journey has never been a one-size-fits-all experience. For some it might be a turn to Ayurveda or yoga, for others meditation, breathwork, energy healing or newer takes on emotional and holistic wellbeing. As India’s wellness ecosystem continues to grow, so does the number of practitioners, philosophies and practices competing for attention.But in an industry where visibility can sometimes trump credibility, knowing who to trust can be daunting. Social media has helped discover wellness practices, but also created the challenge of separating real experience and impact from fleeting fads. As the ecosystem expands, the need is no longer simply for more options, but for greater structure, transparency and accountability.The TOI Healing India Forum 2026 is a confluence of voices from across holistic healing, wellness, integrative health, mindfulness and conscious living. The Forum seeks to acknowledge practitioners and institutions that are contributing in a meaningful way to India’s ever-evolving wellness landscape, while creating a platform for conversations around responsible and credible healing practices.What are the categories?The Forum covers 35 categories across eight disciplines:Energy and Frequency Healing includes Sound Healing & Vibrational Therapy, Chakra Healing & Energy Balancing, Reiki & Energy Healing, Crystal Healing and Pranic Healing.Consciousness and Soul Work includes Past Life Regression Therapy, Akashic Records & Soul Reading, Inner Child & Emotional Healing, Consciousness Expansion & Awakening Work and Soul Coaching / Spiritual Mentorship (Soul Sensei-type work).Mind and Subconscious Therapies includes Hypnotherapy, Emotional Freedom Technique (EFT), Mindfulness & Meditation Therapy and Somatic & Trauma Release Therapy.Group and Collective Healing includes Group Healing Circles, Family Constellation Therapy, Breathwork Circles & Group Facilitation and Women-Centric Healing Circles.Body-Based and Traditional Therapies include Chiropractic Therapy, Acupuncture Therapy, Reflexology & Acupressure, Ayurvedic-Based Therapeutic Healing and Naturopathy & Detox Therapy.Creative and Sensory Healing includes Art Therapy and Color Therapy & Sensory Healing.Yoga Excellence Awards includes Yoga Guru, Yoga Studio, Yoga Therapist and Emerging Yoga Teacher of the Year. It also includes Best Corporate Yoga Program, Most Innovative Yoga Initiative and Lifetime Contribution to Yoga Excellence.Wellness Visionaries Awards includes Healer of the Year, Rising Star Healer and Wellness Author/Content Creator of the Year.Who can participate?The Forum is open to both individuals and institutions, including certified therapists, healers, wellness coaches, wellness centres and retreats. Both emerging and established practitioners can participate, provided they can demonstrate an authentic practice and meaningful impact.Each nomination is assessed through a 100-point evaluation framework, with the greatest weightage given to the depth of healing impact, verified through documented client transformations, accounting for 25 points. On the other hand, training, lineage and experience account for 20 points. Method & structure and verified client testimonials carry 15 points each, followed by ethical considerations and innovation at 10 points each, and community outreach and workshops at 5 points.Entries also undergo editorial and jury verification. The framework limits claims to cure medical conditions and blind spiritual endorsements without structure and unverifiable claims can disqualify. The idea is to put responsible practice alongside recognition.Nominate nowNominations for the TOI Healing India Forum 2026 are open until October 5, 2026. Judging will take place in October, with the award celebration scheduled for October 15, 2026.Healing is deeply personal, and the practices people turn to can be as diverse as their individual journeys. By bringing these varied approaches onto one platform, the Forum seeks to give greater visibility to practitioners, encourage responsible practices and recognise those contributing to India’s changing culture of wellness and conscious living.CLICK HERE to participate now!You use AI every day. articles.title: Song Min-ho: K-pop star convicted of violating military service law
articles.summary: The member of K-pop band Winner was given a suspended prison sentence for repeated absences from his national service work.
articles.body:
A South Korean court has handed a suspended one-year prison sentence to K-pop singer Song Min-ho after he was convicted of violating the country's military service law.

The 33-year-old member of the boy band Winner was found to have been absent multiple times at a community centre in Seoul, where he had worked as a social worker from 2023 to 2024.

All able-bodied men in South Korea have to serve at least 18 months in the military. But some are alternatively assigned as social service personnel for health reasons.

The prison sentence handed on Thursday is suspended for two years. That means he can avoid incarceration if he does not commit any crime during that two-year probationary period.

The court heard that Song, who is also known by his stage name Mino, had recorded 102 unauthorised absences during his 21-month stint as a social service agent.

Military service is a duty to be performed "faithfully", and social service agents are "no exception", the court said.

But the court also noted that Song had admitted to the charges and shown remorse.

Authorities launched an investigation into Song shortly after he was discharged in 2024, when local media reported that he was frequently absent from his social service duties and took excessive sick leave.

Song's supervisor at the social service centre was also given a suspended jail sentence for helping him dodge his duties, including falsifying records to make it look like Song had reported to work.

The conscription of South Korea's entertainers has long been a topic of national public debate.

Gangnam Style singer Psy famously had to enlist twice, once in 2003 and another time in 2007, after a Seoul court ruled that he had neglected his duties by continuing his showbiz activities during his first national service stint.

Steve Yoo, one of the country's biggest pop stars in the 1990s and early 2000s, was embroiled in a national scandal after he was found to have evaded military service in 2002. South Korean authorities banned him from the country after he renounced his citizenship and became a US national shortly before he was due to serve in the military.

Going on hiatus to serve in the military is often a threat for budding careers in South Korea's fast-moving entertainment industry. But the evasion of military service also comes with intense public scrutiny and legal repercussions.

Ahead of the ruling on Thursday, Song told reporters that he regretted his actions and was "sorry toward the people who gave me so much love", Seoul Economic Daily reported.

But he did not answer a question about whether he would re-enlist to serve the mandatory duty.

articles.title: AI-powered glasses give me independence, says blind Cheshire farmer
articles.summary: Dave Cragg, who began to lose his sight at the age of 10, can even read books using the technology.
articles.body:
For the family of visually impaired chicken farmer Dave Cragg, his decision to buy AI-powered smart glasses for his 65th birthday delivered a magical moment.

"It was the first birthday - and I am 33 - [that] I have ever seen my dad be able to read a birthday card," said his eldest daughter Philippa Wilcox.

Cragg, who began losing his sight aged 10 and now has very limited peripheral vision, had initially doubted what benefit the glasses would bring. They have also proven controversial amid concerns about covert recording .

But the camera in the frames, which links to apps on his phone, has enabled Cragg from Wybunbury, Cheshire, to become "a lot more independent" than he had been in the past.

"They can really enhance your life basically," he added.

Alongside the ability to use the camera lens to read things like books and menus out loud, he can also make use of connected apps to navigate the world around him despite living with rod-cone dystrophy - a condition which affects cells in the retina .

One such app called Be My Eyes is staffed by volunteers who, via the glasses, can describe what surrounds Cragg.

"If I was looking for something and didn't know where it was, they could tell me exactly where it was," he said.

And with growing concerns around the rise and risks of AI , he said this technology was "a clear demonstration of how good and useful AI can be".

His eldest daughter Wilcox, who works alongside him on the family poultry farm as well as acting as his support worker, said the Meta glasses and AI-based apps help increase his independence.

"It's nice that he's got the option where he can do some things like reading, checking things, finding things... all of those little things we naturally do without thinking," she said.

The technology also provides peace of mind when he takes the dogs for a walk near their home or is working in the fields, Wilcox added.

"If you were living on your own as a blind person, they would be invaluable," Cragg said.

articles.title: A South Carolina family raised cattle and horses on its farm for generations; in 2025, it permanently protected 2,000 acres from development in the largest such deal in Laurens County's history
articles.summary: A South Carolina family has permanently protected 2,000 acres of farmland, forests and waterways that had remained in private ownership for generations.
articles.body: A South Carolina family has permanently protected 2,000 acres of farmland, forests and waterways that had remained in private ownership for generations. The Creekland Farms property in Laurens County was placed under a conservation easement in 2025, preventing future development while allowing the landowners to continue using it for agriculture, forestry and recreation. The Nature Conservancy described the agreement as the largest conservation easement in Laurens County’s history. The farm once supported champion Hereford and Polled Shorthorn cattle, Rhode Island Red chickens and thoroughbred horses. Today, its fields and forests remain connected to the 170,000-acre Enoree District of the Sumter National Forest, creating a protected landscape in a rapidly growing part of South Carolina. Read on to know more:A family farm under pressureCreekland Farms sits in Laurens County, an area located between Greenville, Spartanburg and Columbia. The property’s rural setting has remained important to the family, but the region is experiencing rapid growth and increasing development pressure. The Nature Conservancy said Laurens County is the third-fastest-growing county in South Carolina’s Upstate region. As new homes, roads and commercial areas spread across the region, large connected areas of farmland and forest are becoming more difficult to preserve.The family’s decision was influenced partly by the farm’s proximity to several growing cities. Keeping the property rural required a long-term commitment because future owners could otherwise face strong financial incentives to sell land for development. Rather than transferring the farm to a public agency, the family chose a conservation easement. This legal agreement permanently limits development rights while allowing the property to remain privately owned and managed.What the conservation easement is all aboutA conservation easement is a voluntary legal agreement to preserve a property’s important natural, agricultural or scenic features. The landowner retains title to the property but certain activities are permanently restricted including large-scale development or subdivision. At Creekland Farms, the easement allows the family to continue using the land for forestry, agriculture and recreation. The property can remain a working farm rather than becoming a public park or a preserve closed to all private activity. The agreement protects the farm’s rural character while giving the owners flexibility to manage the land according to their needs. Cattle, horses, forests, lakes and fields can remain part of the property’s future.The Nature Conservancy helped secure the easement and described it as a way for a family’s values to continue across generations. Conservation agreements of this type can allow landowners to maintain control while preventing future changes that would permanently alter the landscape.A history of animals and agricultureFor multiple generations, Creekland Farms was a place where the family raised animals and managed a working agricultural property. The farm was known for champion Hereford and Polled Shorthorn cattle, breeds valued for their strength, quality and importance to cattle production. The family also raised Rhode Island Red chickens and thoroughbred horses. These animals were part of a wider rural tradition in which farms served as both businesses and family homes.Agriculture land can be more than fields for crops. Farming may be done in pastures, barns, wooded areas, ponds and streams, which are also home to wildlife. Creekland Farms’ conservation easement protects this blend of working land and natural areas. It ensures that the property can continue to be used productively without being divided into residential developments or commercial sites.Connected to a larger forestOne of the property’s most important features is its connection to the Enoree District of the Sumter National Forest. The district covers approximately 170,000 acres and provides a large surrounding landscape of forest, streams and wildlife habitat. Connected properties are especially valuable for conservation because animals and plants often require more space than a single protected parcel can provide. Forest connections allow wildlife to move, find food and respond to changing conditions.The 2,000 acres at Creekland Farms add privately protected land to the broader public forest landscape. Although the farm remains privately owned, the easement reduces the risk that development will fragment the surrounding area. The property’s waterways and forested areas also contribute to water quality and local environmental health. Undeveloped land can help filter rainfall, reduce runoff and provide shade along streams and ponds.Balancing growth and conservationThe agreement comes at a time when Laurens County is trying to accommodate new residents while retaining the rural landscapes that define much of the region. Growth can bring jobs, services and investment, but it can also increase traffic, strain infrastructure and remove farmland. Protecting large properties helps create a balance between those competing pressures. Development can continue in appropriate locations, while farms, forests and waterways remain available to support food production, wildlife and community well-being.Dale Threatt-Taylor, executive director of the Upstate South Carolina office of The Nature Conservancy, said the county’s fields, forests and waterways were under considerable pressure from growth. He credited the family’s long-term vision with protecting the property permanently, as per the report.The agreement also demonstrates that conservation does not always require government ownership. Private landowners can play a major role in protecting South Carolina’s landscapes when they choose to restrict development on their property.A decision intended to last foreverThe conservation easement is permanent, meaning its restrictions remain in place even if the property changes hands. Future owners will be able to manage the farm, forest and recreational areas, but they will not be able to develop the land in ways prohibited by the agreement. That permanence was central to the family’s decision. The owners wanted the farm’s rural character and natural resources to survive beyond the current generation.For a family property, such a decision can carry emotional as well as financial significance. It protects the places where animals were raised, family members worked and generations built memories. The Creekland Farms agreement now gives those values legal protection. The land can continue to support agriculture, forestry, wildlife and recreation while remaining part of a larger rural landscape.A model for family landownersThe protection of Creekland Farms shows how conservation easements can help families keep land in private hands without leaving it vulnerable to future development. The agreement does not freeze the property in time. Instead, it allows the farm to remain active while setting clear limits on how the land can change.For Laurens County, the deal preserves one of its largest remaining private rural properties. For the family, it provides a way to carry forward a commitment to farming and open space.As South Carolina’s Upstate continues to grow, decisions like this will become increasingly important. The future of the region will not be shaped only by new buildings and roads, but also by the farms, forests and waterways that communities choose to protect.Creekland Farms now stands as a lasting example of that choice.
